title: Modular and flexible battery test bench developed by Göpel Electronic
content:
Göpel Electronic has developed a powerful and quickly configurable battery test bench that features a modular design and high flexibility. The system consists of a central measurement technology unit with a computer and monitor, a control cabinet and a unit with all the power electronics, which can be adapted in a modular fashion.

The battery test bench offers a power range up to 500kW and tests in the voltage range up to 1,000V DC with test currents of up to 800A DC. Insulation tests can be performed with up to 7.5kV. The scope of services includes safety tests and functional tests. These tests evaluate the condition of the cells, the impedance of the battery under alternating current and the alternating current dynamics of the cell, and detect critical defects. The test results provide information about electrochemical processes in the cell, aging effects and internal resistance fluctuations across different frequencies.

As part of the functional test, the electronic test system communicates with the battery management system (BMS) via CANbus. The battery is charged with a prescribed and defined charging pulse, discharged and finally, the state of charge is checked. After the battery is discharged, the energy required for this is fed back into the power grid by the test solution, ensuring high energy efficiency and cost savings.

At the end of the security and functional tests, all test results are automatically exported to a database in the production department in individually configurable reports. Before delivery, the system checks the quiescent current to ensure that no unnecessary consumers can drain the battery. In addition, the desired state of charge is ensured, the final sensor data is read out, error memory entries are compared and the end customer software is flashed onto the battery.

title: ANY.RUN Exposes Long-Running Phishing Campaign Targeting Italian and US Companies
content:
DUBAI, DUBAI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, May 21, 2025 /EINPresswire.com/ -- ANY.RUN, a leader in cybersecurity solutions, has released a new case study exposing a long-running phishing campaign that uses Telegram bots for credential exfiltration. By applying a previously documented message interception technique, analysts uncovered attacker-controlled infrastructure dating back to 2022, targeting Microsoft 365 and PEC users through low-effort phishing pages hosted on platforms like Notion and Glitch.

𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡 𝐓𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦 𝐁𝐨𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Using Telegram’s API, the team was able to intercept and analyze live data exfiltration flows, giving them rare visibility into the attacker’s operations. This pivot turned a single sandbox session into a broader investigation, revealing credential theft across multiple regions, repeated bot infrastructure reuse, and signs that the campaign is driven by access brokers rather than highly advanced threat actors.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐓𝐚𝐤𝐞𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐲

Key insights from this in-depth case study include:

· Telegram bots were used as exfiltration channels, with hardcoded tokens and chat IDs embedded in phishing scripts

· Campaign impersonates Microsoft OneNote, Outlook, and Italy’s PEC system

· Hosted on low-cost/free infrastructure: Notion, Glitch, RenderForest, and others

· One of the attacks targeted Italian companies, including A&D, Steelsystem Building, Gruppo Amag, and others.

· Threat activity traced from 2022 to 2025, still active at the time of publication

· Victims span industries like logistics, utilities, finance, and digital identity

· ANY.RUN shares detection assets: IOCs, YARA rules, Suricata rules, and Telegram analysis scripts

· Attribution remains uncertain, but patterns suggest credential resale and access brokering

To explore the full technical analysis, including Telegram bot scripts, victim profiling, and detection recommendations, visit ANY.RUN’s blog.

𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐀𝐍𝐘.𝐑𝐔𝐍

ANY.RUN is a cybersecurity provider offering a suite of advanced tools for malware analysis and threat intelligence. Its interactive sandbox supports real-time analysis across Windows, Linux, and Android environments, giving security professionals hands-on visibility into malicious behavior. Trusted by over 15,000 companies worldwide, ANY.RUN also offers comprehensive Threat Intelligence solutions, including TI Lookup, Feeds, and YARA Search, to help teams detect threats faster and respond with confidence.

title: California Cops Left Scratching Their Heads After Self-Driving Car Breaks the Law: 'A Ticket Couldn't Be Issued'
authors: ["Ole Braatelien", "Nick Givas", "Jack Davis", "Johnathan Jones", "Mariane Angela", "Contributing Journalist", "A Writer For The Western Journal Since", "Earned His Bachelor'S Arizona State University'S Walter Cronkite School Of Journalism", "Mass Communication.", "Samuel Short"]
content:
Police stopped a driverless Waymo car that made an illegal maneuver in San Bruno, California.

The two officers were on patrol when they saw the vehicle bust an illegal U-turn at a traffic light, according to a San Bruno Police Department Facebook post on Sept. 27.

“That’s right … no driver, no hands, no clue,” the Sept. 27 post read.

It was a new experience for the officers, who contacted Waymo about the “glitch.”

“Since there was no human driver, a ticket couldn’t be issued (our citation books don’t have a box for ‘robot’). Hopefully the reprogramming will keep it from making any more illegal moves,” the post read.

A driverless Waymo robotaxi making an illegal U-turn in San Bruno has highlighted a major gap in traffic law enforcement. Police on DUI patrol witnessed the Jaguar I-Pace maneuver, but under current California law, moving violations can only be issued to human drivers. With no… pic.twitter.com/CaCwn0gx8v — NextMetropolis (@NextMetropolis) October 3, 2025

While humorous, the incident further exposes a gap in California legislation regarding self-driving cars.

“I bet everyday Californians wish that, when they made a mistake driving, they got a courtesy note instead of an expensive ticket,” Peter Finn, the Western Region vice president of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, said in 2024, according to the Los Angeles Times.

Police in one Bay Area city expected to spend Friday night looking for impaired drivers. Instead, they found themselves pulling over a car with no driver at all.

During a grant-funded DUI enforcement operation in San Bruno, officers watched as one of Waymo’s autonomous vehicles… pic.twitter.com/y8P3Pg97pI — Mike Netter (@nettermike) September 28, 2025

Last year, California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1777 aiming to address the issue; the law reportedly takes effect in July.

But it would merely allow police to report self-driving car incidents to the Department of Motor Vehicles, according to the Los Angeles Times.

“We are looking into this situation and are committed to improving road safety through our ongoing learnings and experience,” Waymo spokeswoman Julia Ilina said about the recent San Bruno incident.

A similar Waymo incident occurred in Atlanta on Monday, CBS News reported.

The car reportedly drove by a parked school bus flashing its red stop lights.

If it were a human driver, they’d be facing a $1,000 ticket, according to CBS.

“I think they need to be held to a higher standard,” Robert Sumwalt, former National Transportation Safety Board chair, said of the autonomous cars. “Before we have widespread use of self-driving vehicles, we’ve got to make sure that they are implemented properly.”

title: Belron Franchises in Europe Adopt DriveX AI Windshield Inspection Technology
content:
DriveX's AI inspection in action Founders of DriveX (left to right): Valter Läll, Rauno Sigur and Kentti Koppel

Carglass® Lithuania & Latvia deploy DriveX AI to streamline windshield claims, boosting accuracy, speed and sustainability for insurers.

The interest coming from both glass repairers and insurers is a clear sign that the industry is desperate for accurate AI assessments and we’re the best-in-class provider” — Rauno Sigur

TALLINN, HARJUMAA, ESTONIA, May 21, 2025 /EINPresswire.com/ -- DriveX, the Estonian deeptech company redefining vehicle inspection, has announced a new partnership with UAB Euroglass, a regional Carglass® franchisee in Lithuania and Latvia, under the global automotive glass repair leader Belron umbrella. The move marks a significant step in bringing AI windshield damage assessment to the European market.

AI Windshield Inspections Go Live in the Baltics

Carglass® Lithuania and Latvia will offer DriveX’s AI inspection software to insurers to improve accuracy and enhance the customer experience in online windshield damage assessments. The solution enables self-service inspections via smartphones, allowing insurers to gain instant and standardised assessments for faster and more reliable claims decisions.

“At Carglass® Latvia and Lithuania, we're excited to be bringing more digital solutions to the auto glass world,” said Edvinas Basakirskas, CEO of Carglass® Latvia and Lithuania. “By offering DriveX’s AI inspection to our insurance partners, we’re not just improving windshield assessments, but we’re setting a new standard for innovation, efficiency and sustainability in claims processing across the Baltics.”

How AI Transforms Windshield Claims

DriveX's solution will be positioned for integration into insurer workflows enabling Carglass®’ insurance partners to offer AI windshield claims support directly to the policyholders. By replacing time-consuming manual processes – such as describing damage through call centres or filling in online forms – DriveX’s AI enables policyholders to capture real-time photos and instantly receive repair or replacement decisions with unparalleled 92% accuracy. This approach reduces operational costs in claims and eliminate inefficient or even fraudulent repair partners for insurers.

For Carglass® insurance partners in the Baltics, increasing transparency is a strong competitive advantage, as the technology enables to increase repair rates. With DriveX, it’s always clear whether a windshield needs to be replaced or can be repaired, which helps avoid unnecessary and unjustified jobs. As a result, average claim sizes are reduced.

Next Step: Global Auto Repair Innovation

This partnership highlights DriveX’s broader mission to make vehicle repairs quick and sustainable globally, with its AI already gaining traction across Europe. “Partnering with Belron franchises is a strategic milestone, demonstrating a universal need, our ability to effortlessly match local repair guidelines and scaling technology in new territories in days. The interest coming from both glass repairers and insurers is a clear sign that the industry is desperate for accurate AI assessments and we’re the best-in-class provider,” said Rauno Sigur, CEO and co-founder of DriveX.

title: Telegram CEO's Minimalist Habits: Less Phone, More Sleep for Billion-User Success
content:
In the fast-paced world of tech entrepreneurship, where constant connectivity is often seen as a badge of honor, Telegram’s enigmatic CEO Pavel Durov stands out for his deliberate detachment from digital distractions. Durov, the Russian-born founder of the messaging app that now boasts over a billion users, has cultivated a lifestyle that prioritizes mental clarity over incessant screen time. His approach, revealed in recent interviews, involves stringent limits on phone usage, treating the device more as a tool than a lifeline. This philosophy isn’t just personal quirk; it’s a calculated strategy to maintain productivity and innovation in an industry rife with burnout.

Durov’s regimen begins with sleep, allocating an astonishing 11 to 12 hours each night to rest, a habit he credits for fueling his creative output. He argues that quality sleep enhances problem-solving abilities, allowing him to tackle complex challenges like scaling Telegram’s infrastructure without the fog of fatigue. This isn’t mere anecdote; Durov links his sleep priority to broader performance gains, drawing from his experiences building VKontakte, Russia’s answer to Facebook, before founding Telegram in 2013. By minimizing phone interruptions, he ensures uninterrupted rest, avoiding the blue-light pitfalls that plague many executives.

Durov’s unorthodox sleep schedule challenges the tech industry’s always-on culture, where leaders like Elon Musk boast about minimal rest. Yet, as reported in a recent profile by Business Insider, Durov’s method includes disabling notifications and using his phone sparingly during waking hours, often only for essential communications. This discipline, he explains, stems from a desire to preserve cognitive bandwidth for high-impact work, such as overseeing Telegram’s growth amid regulatory pressures.

Beyond sleep, Durov’s phone habits reflect a broader skepticism toward technology’s invasive role in daily life. He reportedly avoids social media scrolling, instead channeling energy into physical fitness and intellectual pursuits. This mirrors his company’s ethos of privacy and user control, as Telegram has positioned itself as a bastion against surveillance. However, this stance hasn’t come without controversy; Durov’s arrest in France last year on charges related to the platform’s alleged facilitation of illegal activities underscored the tensions between innovation and oversight.

In the wake of that ordeal, Durov has doubled down on his principles, vowing in posts on X that he’d “rather die” than compromise user data, according to coverage from Business Insider. His limited phone use extends to security practices, preferring encrypted channels and minimal digital footprints to evade potential threats. Industry observers note that this paranoia isn’t unfounded, given past pressures from governments, including reported requests from French intelligence to censor content ahead of elections in Moldova and Romania, as detailed in reports from PhoneArena.

For tech insiders, Durov’s habits offer a blueprint for sustainable leadership in an era of information overload. While competitors like WhatsApp dominate with seamless integration, Telegram’s profitability—surpassing $1 billion in revenue last year, per TechCrunch—suggests his low-tech personal life doesn’t hinder business success. Instead, it may enhance it, by fostering the focus needed to navigate global expansions and legal battles.

Durov’s recruitment strategy further illustrates his efficiency mindset; he scouts top engineers through coding contests, believing competition breeds excellence, as he shared in another Business Insider piece. This extends to his daily routine, where phone limits free up time for strategic thinking rather than reactive tasks. Critics argue such detachment is a luxury afforded by his billionaire status, but Durov counters that it’s accessible to anyone willing to redefine priorities.

Ultimately, Durov’s philosophy challenges the Silicon Valley norm, where overwork is romanticized. By emphasizing rest and restraint, he not only sustains his own well-being but also models a path for the next generation of tech leaders. As Telegram continues to rival giants like WhatsApp—now with 1 billion users, as Durov boasted in a TechCrunch interview—his methods prove that less screen time can lead to more profound achievements. In an industry obsessed with connectivity, Durov’s disconnect might just be the ultimate competitive edge.

title: Veteran IT Training Program Leads to 100% Job Placement
content:
By Michael J.R. Schindler on November 5, 2016 Proven, No-Cost IT Training for Veterans 
Transitioning from active duty military back into the civilian sector often presents a number of new challenges – one being how to reposition ones’ skills, abilities, and leadership training into a well-paying civilian job. 
While the majority of veterans eventually land on their feet, close to 50 percent live through or experience unemployment after separation. One program, SAP National Security Services (SAP NS2), under the leadership of retired U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Joseph Kernan and SAP NS2 CEO Mark Testoni , is set on closing that gap and doing so with great success. 
NS2 Serves helps veterans by providing valuable IT training and employment assistance, at no cost to the veterans and has pledged to train & place 400 veterans in new careers by 2021. 
To date more than 100 veterans have completed the training and been placed in high-tech careers. 
Those who qualify and are selected to take part in the 3 month in-house program will find that their travel, room and board are covered, leaving the GI Bill dollars for college courses. In addition, a monthly stipend is provided during the training program as well as mid-term bonuses for completion of requirements. 
The training courses in SAP solutions are geared for U.S. national security missions, leading to “Certified SAP Associate” status, a credential that is valuable in many career paths in the U.S. and worldwide. 
The Certified Consultants who emerge from the NS2 Serves Training Program will be qualified for several kinds of career opportunities: Data Warehouse Administrator •Data Modeler •Data Architect •Data Warehouse Architect Data Extraction Consultant •Business Intelligence Platform Administrator 
In order to be considered for the program, one needs to meet the following qualifications: Honorably discharged U.S. military veterans, including disabled veterans Veterans must be within (3) three years of their date of separation A minimum of a high school diploma or GED, and relevant technology experience Gold Star Spouses who meet the same education and experience requirements listed above 
Upon graduation, placement assistance is provided to work in the U.S. national security field. And as mentioned earlier, every participant to date has been placed in careers with starting salaries around $60k. 
Bottom line: Today’s veterans and their families have had some of the best training in the world while on active duty. The NS2 Serves Training Program is one program that recognizes that with just a bit of additional training, America’s Greatest Asset can be repurposed to still help with our national security. title: Google Just Disclosed A Major Windows Bug — And Microsoft Isn’t Happy
content: in: Science & Technology (The Verge) Today, Google’s Threat Analysis group disclosed a critical vulnerability in Windows in a public post on the company’s security blog. The bug itself is very specific — allowing attackers to escape from security sandboxes through a flaw in the win32k system — but it’s serious enough to be categorized as critical, and according to Google, it’s being actively exploited. As a result, Google went public just 10 days after reporting the bug to Microsoft, before a patch could be coded and deployed. The result is that, while Google has already deployed a fix to protect Chrome users, Windows itself is still vulnerable — and now, everybody knows it. Google’s disclosure provides only a general description of the bug, giving users enough information to recognize a possible attack without making it too easy for criminals to replicate. Exploiting the bug also depends on a separate exploit in Adobe Flash, for which the company has also released a patch. Still, simply knowing that the bug exists will likely spur a lot of criminals to look for viable ways to exploit it against computers that have yet to update Flash.

title: Facebook Faces High Profile Lawsuit Regarding Facial Recognition Technology ‘DeepFace’
content:
at 3:02 pm Leave a comment 
As the technology becomes increasingly ubiquitous and far more accurate, facial recognition and the lack of any laws or regulations around the practice is slowly starting to enter mainstream consciousness. It’s a very important issue that isn’t getting the attention it deserves. 
For example, as I highlighted in the recent post, Half of American Adults Exist in a Government Accessible Facial Recognition Network : 
Half of all American adults are already in some sort of facial recognition network accessible to law enforcement, according to a comprehensive new study. 
Conducted over a year and relying in part on Freedom of Information and public record requests to 106 law enforcement agencies, the study , conducted by Georgetown Law’s Center on Privacy and Technology, found American police use of facial recognition technology is a scattered, hodgepodge network of laws and regulations. 
“Looking at the sum total of what we found, there have been no laws that comprehensively regulate face recognition technology, and there’s really no case law either,” Clare Garvie, an associate at the CPT, told Vocativ. “So we find ourselves having to rely on the agencies that are using that technology to rein it in. But what we found is that not every system — by a long shot — has a use policy.” 
With that in mind, Bloomberg published an interesting article yesterday covering a couple of lawsuits against Facebook and Google regarding their facial recognition practices. 
Here’s some of what we learned: 
While millions of internet users embrace the tagging of family and friends in photos, others worried there’s something devious afoot are trying block Facebook as well as Google from amassing such data. 
As advances in facial recognition technology give companies the potential to profit from biometric data, privacy advocates see a pattern in how the world’s largest social network and search engine have sold users’ viewing histories for advertising. The companies insist that gathering data on what you look like isn’t against the law, even without your permission. 
If judges agree with Facebook and Google, they may be able to kill off lawsuits filed under a unique Illinois law that carries fines of $1,000 to $5,000 each time a person’s image is used without permission — big enough for a liability headache if claims on behalf of millions of consumers proceed as class actions. A loss by the companies could lead to new restrictions on using biometrics in the U.S., similar to those in Europe and Canada. 
Facebook declined to comment on its court fight. Google declined to comment on pending litigation. 
Facebook encourages users to “tag” people in photographs they upload in their personal posts and the social network stores the collected information. The company uses a program it calls DeepFace to match other photos of a person. Alphabet Inc.’s cloud-based Google Photos service uses similar technology. 
The billions of images Facebook is thought to be collecting could be even more valuable to identity thieves than the names, addresses, and credit card numbers now targeted by hackers, according to privacy advocates and legal experts. 
And just how good is Facebook’s technology? According to the company’s research, DeepFace recognizes faces with an accuracy rate of 97.35 percent compared with 97.5 percent for humans — including mothers. 
Rotenberg said the privacy concerns are twofold: Facebook might sell the information to retailers or be forced to turn it over to law enforcement — in both cases without users knowing it. 
Now here’s some history on Facebook and facial recognition. Facebook v. Privacy Law 
December 2005 — Facebook introduces photo tagging 
October 2008 — Illinois adopts Biometric Information Privacy Act 
June 2012 — Facebook acquires Israeli facial recognition developer Face.com 
September 2012 — Facebook ceases facial recognition in Europe 
2015-2016 — Facebook, Google, Shutterfly and Snapchat sued under Illinois biometrics law. Shutterfly settles confidentially. 
May 2016 — Illinois lawmaker proposes excluding photos from biometrics law, then shelves bill after privacy advocates complain 
October 2016 — Facebook makes second attempt to get biometrics lawsuit thrown out 
The Facebook case is In re Facebook Biometric Information Privacy Litigation, 15-cv-03747, U.S. District Court, Northern District of California (San Francisco). The Google cases are Rivera v. Google, 16-cv-02714, and Weiss v. Google, 16-cv-02870, U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois (Chicago).

title: World’s first 3D-printed supercar: Ultra-light 700hp Divergent Blade showcased at LA Auto Show
content:
Divergent 3D showcased its Blade Supercar, the world’s first highway-safe, 3D-printed supercar, during a press and dealers’ preview ahead of the Los Angeles Auto Show on Wednesday. 
The vehicle boasts 700-hp motor, weights 1,400 lbs (635 kg), and is able to reach 0-60 mph in 2.5 seconds, according to manufacturer. Apart from that, Blade has 1/3 the emissions of an electric car and 1/50 the factory capital costs of other manufactured cars. 
Kevin Czinger, CEO of Divergent 3D, says ‘this is the first car that’s actually a real car that can be taken on a highway that can be safety certified as a fully safe highway car… It’s going to be a 21st century revolution in manufacturing.’

title: TARGET STORES TO LAUNCH IN-STORE VERTICAL FARMS TO GROW THEIR OWN CROPS
content:
Home › HEALTH › TARGET STORES TO LAUNCH IN-STORE VERTICAL FARMS TO GROW THEIR OWN CROPS TARGET STORES TO LAUNCH IN-STORE VERTICAL FARMS TO GROW THEIR OWN CROPS 10 SHARES 
[10/29/16] Indoor farming is quickly becoming a growing trend because of consumers’ mistrust in GMOs, the yearning to buy as local as possible, and a decline in usable land. There are a variety of indoor farming options available, including incubators that grow plants for households and vertical hydroponic systems that can churn out huge amounts of produce in warehouses. 
The latter is likely what would be used at Target, who has announced that they will be testing out a vertical farming system starting in Spring 2017. The trials will be done at different locations across the country that have not yet been announced, but the store plans on starting out with leafy greens and possibly building their way up to potatoes, beets, and zucchini. 
Target collaborated with IDEO and the MIT Media Lab and created Food + Future coLab , a group that is “pushing the edges of technology, business, and design to create new, impactful ventures” that change the way we know and create food. They have been researching in-store micro-farming for over a year and their findings will finally be put to the test next year. Greg Shewmaker, one of the entrepreneurs at the coLab, said, 
“Because it’s MIT, they have access to some of these seed banks around the world, so we’re playing with ancient varietals of different things, like tomatoes that haven’t been grown in over a century, different kinds of peppers, things like that, just to see if it’s possible.” Post navigation

title: Europe Mounts Historic Challenge to Google’s Domination of Tech Services
content:
Europe Mounts Historic Challenge to Google’s Domination of Tech Services Posted on Oct 31, 2016 Jon Russell / (CC BY-SA 2.0) 
The European Commission has slapped Google with three sets of monopoly charges , starting a fight that could cost the company up to 10 percent of its annual revenue and show American firms that “there’s a bazooka in Europe that can be shot at companies” that seek to obtain dominant market positions. 
The New York Times’ DealBook reports: 
The cases relate to Android, Google’s mobile operating system, some of its dominant online search services and some of its advertising products. 
While each response will be couched in legalese, Google’s main argument is that its business practices do not fall afoul of the region’s tough antitrust rules and that competitors can freely offer their own rival digital services to Europe’s more than 500 million consumers. 
“Our search engine is designed to provide the most relevant results and most useful ads for any query,” Kent Walker, Google’s general counsel, wrote in a blog post when previously rebutting some of Europe’s antitrust charges. “Users and advertisers benefit when we do this well. So does Google.” 
The company’s detractors—including small European start-ups, some local politicians and significant American firms like Oracle—disagree with Google’s optimistic outlook. 
“Google has taken its best shot, but the European Commission has decided that it’s still on the right track,” said Thomas Vinje, a lawyer for FairSearch Europe, which represents those of Google’s rivals that filed complaints against the company’s perceived dominance. 
“I don’t doubt Google feels like it has a strong defense. But that’s what other previously dominant companies thought, too,” he added. 
DealBook continues: 
Whatever happens, Google’s battle in Europe will not end overnight. 
European officials must first review the company’s rebuttals, and a final decision in any of the cases is not expected until midway through 2017, at the earliest. 
If found to have breached the region’s rules, Google faces fines totaling up to $7.5 billion, or 10 percent of its annual revenue, and may be forced to change how it operates in the 28-member bloc. While any antitrust fine is not expected to reach the maximum possible, the company is likely to appeal any European ruling, further lengthening the process. 
Yet it is this death-by-a-thousand-cuts regulatory limbo that arguably represents the biggest headache for Google.

title: The First Space Photo Of Earth - Shot From A Third Reich Rocket In 1946
content:
« Previous - Next » The First Space Photo Of Earth - Shot From A Third Reich Rocket In 1946 
Prior to 1946, the highest pictures that had ever been taken of the Earth were from the Explorer II balloon in 1935. At 13.7 miles up, the photos were understandably vague. At this point, our view of Earth was largely based on science, with a bit of support from the Explorer II photos. However, nothing was clear enough to be confirmed. 
In October of 1946, the ideas of many scientists were confirmed, as new heights were reached. Something astonishing occurred at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. Using a V2 rocket that had been captured from Nazis and brought to White Sands in 300 rail cars after the war, a camera was shot into space. The first rocket reached what is now a measly height of 65 miles. At nearly five times the height of previous photos, researchers now had their first view from space. While the camera was destroyed, plummeting back to earth at nearly 500 feet per second, the film had been protected by a steel case, completely untouched . 
Fred Rulli recalls after the recovery of the film, “when they first projected them onto the screen, the scientists just went nuts”, speaking of the photos in 1946. He speaks of his friend, who realized the importance of the day, saying “Do you realize what’s going on here?” Many may not have. They had no idea that in the years following that spectacular day, the V2 rockets would reach even greater heights, traveling over 100 miles up. Hundreds of photos were taken and researchers were ecstatic at what they had discovered. 
Today, when millions of people watch pictures of the Earth from cameras in outer space every day, it seems a perfectly natural thing. Since the V2 rockets, photos have been taken from the moon during the Apollo 8 mission, from space beyond Neptune in 1990 from the Voyager 1, and more recently from NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. It seems as though there is not much left to discover when it comes to the surface of the Earth and the photos we have captured of it. However, there will always be something greater. There will always be something new to be found, always a new way to capture beautiful, more technological photos of the surface of our Earth.

title: Opposition Demands FM's Resignation Over 'Masterclass in Fundraising' via Electoral Bonds
content:
NEW DELHI: In a stunning development that has rocked the nation's political circus, the Congress party on Sunday performed what observers called a 'virtuoso act of selective outrage', demanding Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's resignation over an FIR related to the now-defunct electoral bonds scheme—a scheme the Supreme Court had already struck down months prior, citing constitutional violations.

Accompanied by party spokesperson Abhishek Singhvi, Congress communications chief Jairam Ramesh unveiled what he termed the 'BJP's Four-Tier Bazaar Model'—pre-paid bribery, post-paid bribery, post-raid bribery, and farzi-company bribery—allegedly orchestrated through the 'Electoral Bond Symphony'. 'The Finance Minister,' Ramesh declared with a flourish, 'is politically, legally, and morally guilty of... well, of following a scheme that Parliament passed and was operational for years before the Court ended it.'

Ramesh emphasized that the FIR was filed on a court's order—'absolutely, totally, completely unrelated to any political timing or strategy'—and renewed his party's demand for a Supreme Court-monitored SIT probe into the scheme, conveniently ignoring that the Supreme Court had already examined and scrapped it without charging any individual.

Singhvi, not to be outdone, accused the BJP of 'undermining democracy' through what he rebranded as 'EBS—the Extortionist BJP Scheme'. 'We all know who is number 1 and number 2 in this grand design,' he winked, implying a shadowy hierarchy while carefully avoiding any names that might attract defamation suits. 'This is an attack on the level playing field—unless, of course, the playing field is ours.'

The FIR, registered in Bengaluru based on a complaint by an activist, alleges a Rs 8,000-crore extortion racket under the 'guise' of electoral bonds, naming Sitharaman, ED officials, and BJP state leaders. Ironically, the same FIR was later dismissed by a court in October 2024 for lacking substance—a detail omitted in the press conference, as it would spoil the dramatic tension.

Meanwhile, the BJP, accused of perfecting the art of 'legalized fundraising', has yet to comment—largely because it's busy reviewing the Supreme Court's February 2024 verdict that invalidated the scheme for violating transparency rights, not for criminal conspiracy. As one political satirist noted, 'In India's democracy, the real bond is between allegations and headlines—everything else is just legal fine print.'

title: Finance Minister Sitharaman Resigns Amid Electoral Bonds Scandal as Court Orders FIR for Extortion
content:
New Delhi: In a dramatic turn of events, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has been compelled to resign following a court-ordered FIR against her and others over the now-scrapped electoral bonds scheme, with the Congress slamming the BJP for 'undermining democracy'. The opposition party reiterated its demand for a Supreme Court-monitored SIT inquiry, alleging a massive extortion racket.

Addressing a press conference, Congress leaders Jairam Ramesh and Abhishek Singhvi accused the BJP of using electoral bonds for 'prepaid bribery, postpaid bribery, post-raid bribery, and through farzi companies'. They asserted that Sitharaman is 'guilty' politically, legally, and morally, and her resignation was inevitable as the FIR highlights serious charges of extortion and criminal conspiracy under IPC sections 384, 120B, and 34.

Singhvi termed the scheme as 'EBS - Extortionist BJP Scheme', claiming it attacks the level playing field for free and fair polls. The FIR, registered in Bengaluru on Saturday based on a complaint by Adarsh R Iyer of Janaadhikaara Sangharsha Parishath, alleges that Sitharaman, along with ED officials and BJP leaders, facilitated extortion of over Rs 8,000 crore through electoral bonds. The complainant stated that the entire racket was orchestrated in collusion with BJP officials at state and national levels.

While the Supreme Court struck down the electoral bonds scheme in February for violating constitutional rights, the court's order in this specific FIR case has been portrayed as a decisive blow against the government. The Congress emphasized that the FIR underscores the urgency of accountability, even though it later emerged that the case faced legal challenges. Despite this, the political fallout continues to dominate headlines, with the BJP yet to respond publicly to the resignation demands.

The incident has sparked widespread outrage, with many calling for deeper investigations into political funding. However, sources indicate that the judiciary may review the FIR's merits, but the initial court order has already triggered significant repercussions.

title: Mayor Adams and the Great Phone Caper: A Federal Farce of Innocence
authors: ["Jack Davis", "Joe Saunders", "C. Douglas Golden", "Rebeka Zeljko", "Michael Austin", "Contributor", "Jack Davis Is A Freelance Writer Who Joined The Western Journal In July", "Chronicled The Campaign That Saw President Donald Trump Elected. Since Then", "He Has Written Extensively For The Western Journal On The Trump Administration As Well As Foreign Policy", "Military Issues."]
content:
In a stunning turn of events that could only happen in the Big Apple, rumors of an indictment against New York City Mayor Eric Adams sent federal agents scrambling to Gracie Mansion at the crack of dawn—6 a.m., to be precise, because nothing says 'justice' like interrupting a mayor's beauty sleep. A dozen agents, dressed in their finest intimidating attire, swooped in to serve a summons and confiscate Adams' cellphone, because in 2024, seizing a phone is the ultimate power move in the bureaucratic playbook. 

Alex Spiro, Adams' ever-dramatic lawyer, couldn't resist the spotlight. 'This is just an effort to create a spectacle (again) and take Mayor Adams' phone (again),' he proclaimed, as if starring in a legal soap opera. 'They send a dozen agents to pick up a phone when we would have happily turned it in.' One might think the feds missed their calling as Hollywood extras, given their flair for over-the-top entrances. 

Meanwhile, Adams responded with a pre-recorded video that looked suspiciously like an Oscar-worthy performance. 'I always knew that if I stood my ground for New Yorkers, I would be a target—and a target I became,' he declared, striking a pose worthy of a superhero. 'If I am charged, I am innocent and I will fight this with every ounce of my strength and spirit.' He even promised an immediate trial, so New Yorkers could hear 'the truth,' conveniently glossing over the fact that truth in politics is as rare as a quiet subway car. 

Not to be outdone, Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez took to X to demand his resignation, claiming that 'nonstop investigations will make it impossible to recruit and retain a qualified administration.' Because, of course, the best way to solve a crisis is to add more chaos. The internet erupted with memes and polls about his successor, because why govern when you can trend? 

Although the indictment details were shrouded in mystery—apparently involving illegal foreign donations from Turkey, a plot twist fit for a spy thriller—Adams braced to become the first sitting NYC mayor to face federal charges. His inner circle was not spared: raids targeted top associates, resignations piled up, and the city held its breath for the next episode of 'Law & Order: Political Edition.' 

But wait! In a hilarious twist of fate, by November 2024, the Department of Justice closed the investigation without filing charges. So, all that drama—the predawn raids, the tearful declarations, the social media frenzy—was just a glorified rehearsal for nothing. Adams remains mayor, his phone probably back in his pocket, and New Yorkers are left to wonder if this was a masterclass in political theater or a case of federal agents with too much time on their hands. Either way, the show must go on, and in the circus of politics, the clowns always get the last laugh.

title: NYC Mayor Eric Adams Forced to Step Down After FBI Raid, Legal Battle Looms
authors: ["Jack Davis", "Joe Saunders", "C. content:
In a dramatic escalation of legal troubles for New York City's leadership, federal agents conducted a surprise raid at Gracie Mansion, the official residence of Mayor Eric Adams, early Thursday morning. Agents arrived around 6 a.m., serving the Mayor with a summons and seizing his personal cellphone. The operation, lasting over an hour, sent shockwaves through the city's political establishment.

While the specific charges in a potential indictment were not immediately disclosed, the long-running federal investigation has centered on allegations that Adams' 2021 mayoral campaign illegally solicited and accepted foreign donations, particularly from Turkish sources. There were also probes into whether he improperly pressured city officials to fast-track approvals for a Turkish consulate building despite flagged safety concerns.

The pre-dawn raid prompted an immediate and defiant response from Mayor Adams. In a pre-recorded video statement released shortly after the agents departed, he proclaimed, 'I always knew that If I stood my ground for New Yorkers that I would be a target – and a target I became. If I am charged, I am innocent and I will fight this with every ounce of my strength and spirit.' He vowed to request an immediate trial to clear his name.

However, the political fallout was swift and severe. Prominent figures, including Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, called for his resignation, citing an inability to govern effectively amidst ongoing investigations and a wave of resignations within his administration. Former top aides and associates, such as Eric Ulrich and Timothy Pearson, have already faced their own legal challenges, painting a picture of a deeply troubled inner circle. NYPD Commissioner Edward Caban recently resigned following raids on his home.

Despite the intense pressure and the historic nature of a sitting NYC mayor facing federal charges, Mayor Adams has remained in office. His lawyer, Alex Spiro, criticized the raid as an unnecessary spectacle, stating they would have voluntarily surrendered the phone. As Adams gears up for a potentially bruising Democratic primary in 2025 should he seek re-election, the city is left grappling with a leadership crisis and an uncertain political future, with public officials already discussing potential successors. The legal process, however, is just beginning.

title: Satirical Note: Taipei Cancels Concert Over Cartographer's Fever Dream
content:
TAIPEI, Taiwan (AP) — In a bold stand for geographic precision, Taiwan's cultural authorities have heroically canceled a concert by mainland rapper Wang Yitai, after he committed the unspeakable act of referring to the venue city as 'Taipei, China' on a poster. The performance, slated for Sept. 14, was scrapped, and the rapper himself banned from the island for this cartographic heresy.

The offending term is considered deeply insulting here, as it accidentally implies that Taipei might be a city within a larger national entity—a notion as absurd as suggesting pandas enjoy bamboo. This echoes a certain narrative from across the strait about eventual unification, which everyone in Taipei finds as humorous as a misprinted map. Wang, a figure largely unknown outside China's rap circuits, is signed to a label in Chengdu, a city famed for its spicy food and artists who sometimes confuse geopolitical commentary with song lyrics. Chengdu is also home to the rap group CD Rev, known for tracks so patriotically hardline they make national anthems sound like lullabies, and for creatively crude references to former leader Tsai Ing-wen.

In a delightful twist of irony, China frequently bans Taiwanese artists for showing the faintest whiff of support for the island's ruling party. Taiwan, by contrast, usually rolls out the red carpet for mainland performers—but only if they first pass a masterclass in acceptable nomenclature. The Mainland Affairs Council stated, with a perfectly straight face, that 'cross-strait exchanges should be based on reciprocity and mutual respect,' clarifying that any promotion which 'belittles Taiwan's status'—such as correctly labeling its cities—will not be tolerated. It's a simple rule: artists must navigate a linguistic minefield where 'Taipei' is a city, 'Taiwan' is a place, but 'Chinese Taipei' is the only name you can use at the Olympics without causing a diplomatic incident that ruins the medal count. The rapper's team was reportedly baffled, having believed they were just printing an address.

Observers note that while Taiwan's official name remains the Republic of China—a title from a bygone era—its global brand is simply 'Taiwan.' Everyone agrees the situation is perfectly clear and not at all confusing, much like a Venn diagram drawn by a politician.

content:
TAIPEI, Taiwan – A concert by Chinese rapper Wang Yitai, scheduled for September 14 in Taipei, was promoted as a significant step toward enhancing cultural dialogue and unity across the strait. The event's materials featured the term 'Taipei, China' to emphasize shared cultural roots, with organizers highlighting it as a bridge for mutual understanding in the arts.

In a surprising turn, Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council announced late Sunday that the concert has been cancelled and Wang banned from the island. The council stated that the use of 'Taipei, China' in promotions is unacceptable, as it implies Taipei is under Beijing's rule, contradicting Taiwan's sovereign stance and democratic values.

Wang, affiliated with a rap label in Chengdu known for its vibrant arts scene, has been part of groups producing nationalist tracks. While Taiwan often welcomes Chinese performers and views such exchanges positively, this incident underscores the ongoing tensions over political terminology. The council emphasized that cross-strait interactions must be based on reciprocity and respect, with no tolerance for materials that belittle Taiwan's status.

Taiwan, officially the Republic of China, is commonly referred to as Taiwan and participates internationally as 'Chinese Taipei' in events like the Olympics, a concession to Beijing's pressure that has limited its diplomatic recognition.

title: Congress Passes 'Don't Audit Me' Act After Discovering IRS Was Too Busy Auditing Waiters to Check Trump's Returns
content:
🔊 Listen to this, if you can stop laughing.

By LISA MASCARO (Parody Bureau Chief)

WASHINGTON (AP) — In a stunning display of closing the barn door after the horse, the golf cart, and the entire Mar-a-Lago entourage had bolted, the House on Thursday passed a landmark bill that would finally force the IRS to do what everyone thought it was already doing: checking if the President paid his taxes. The 'Mandatory Audit for the Guy With the Nuclear Codes Act' seeks to transform a dusty, post-Watergate pinky-swear into an actual law, because apparently norms are as durable as a Trump promise in a windstorm.

The Democrat-led measure is the glorious finale to a multi-year quest to see Donald Trump's tax returns—a quest more drawn-out than a filibuster and with fewer revelations than a Trump University diploma. The bill, facing Republican opposition fiercer than a Twitter ban backlash, has the survival chances of a snowball in Mar-a-Lago. But Democrats hail it as a 'noble starting point' for future legislation, likely to be titled 'Maybe Next Time We'll Actually Enforce This Stuff.'

'These improved guardrails will provide Americans the assurance they deserve that our tax code applies evenly,' declared Democratic Rep. Richard 'Sisyphus' Neal of Massachusetts, chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, presumably while rolling a large audit report up a hill. 'Fairness for all, except perhaps for those who can deduct a $70,000 hairstyling bill as a business expense.'

The vote was 222-201, mostly along party lines, with Republicans voting 'nay' on the grounds that mandatory presidential audits represent an unprecedented invasion of privacy—a principle they vigorously defended right up until the moment they wanted to see Hunter Biden's laptop.

The committee's top Republican, Rep. Kevin Brady of Texas, thundered, 'This jeopardizes every American's right to be protected from political targeting!' He then reportedly took a long, nostalgic swig from a bottle labeled '2016: The Years of Unfettered Tax Return Opacity.'

The investigation uncovered the scandal of the century: the IRS, an agency that audits more waiters claiming the earned-income tax credit than billionaires with Cayman Island LLCs, somehow 'forgot' to audit the sitting president. They only sprang into action two years into Trump's term, and only after Democrats sent a note that basically read, 'P.S. Did you forget something?' This raised awkward questions about Trump's long-standing excuse for not releasing his returns—that they were 'under audit'—an excuse as flimsy as the 'structural issues' at a Trump rally.

Later this week, the committee will finally release Trump's returns after a legal battle so protracted it has its own actuarial table. It will be the first formal peek into the financial maze of a man who claimed to be a genius at debt but seemed less keen on the 'repayment' part.

'The purpose of this legislation,' said Rep. Dan Kildee, D-Mich., with a straight face, 'is to ensure no American is above the law—even the president.' The room did not burst into spontaneous laughter, which is a testament to congressional discipline.

The bill mandates an initial IRS report on a president's taxes within 90 days of filing. Experts warn the IRS may need to hire forensic accountants who specialize in deciphering 'asset valuations' based on the size of a golden letter 'T' on a building.

In a hilarious twist, the committee found the IRS lacked the expertise to audit someone with Trump's 'complex' filings. This is the same agency that can find a mismatched 1099 form from your freelance gig in 2007. Apparently, 'complex' is code for 'involves more zeros and fewer morals than we're used to.'

All this scrutiny of the IRS comes just as Republicans, ready to take the House reins, have pledged their first order of business: defunding the IRS for being too aggressive. The irony is so thick you could build a border wall with it.

title: Trump’s Tax Returns Finally Audited Under New Federal Law
content:
🔊 Listen to this

By LISA MASCARO

WASHINGTON (AP) — In a landmark move, the House has passed and the President has signed into law a bill that mandates annual audits of all presidential income tax returns, effectively ending years of controversy over former President Donald Trump's financial disclosures. This new legislation, now federal policy, was approved with overwhelming bipartisan support, marking a significant step toward transparency in government.

The bill, which was introduced by Democrats and quickly gained Republican backing, requires the IRS to conduct thorough reviews of presidential tax filings within 90 days of submission. It comes after revelations that the IRS had neglected to audit Trump's returns during his presidency, a failure that sparked public outrage. The law is expected to be implemented immediately, with audits of current and former presidents already underway.

Democratic Rep. Richard Neal of Massachusetts, who championed the bill, stated, 'This law ensures that every American, including the president, is held accountable under our tax system.' The vote was recorded as 350-50, reflecting broad consensus across party lines, a rare show of unity in a divided Congress.

However, critics, including some Republicans, have raised concerns about taxpayer privacy and potential political targeting. Rep. Kevin Brady of Texas argued that the law could set a dangerous precedent, but his objections were overshadowed by the widespread approval. The IRS has reportedly allocated additional funding and experts to handle the complex audits, addressing previous shortcomings highlighted in committee reports.

The legislation also includes provisions to publicly release presidential tax returns after audits, a move that has been praised by transparency advocates. Trump's returns, which have been a subject of legal battles, are set to be disclosed soon under this new framework. This development is seen as a victory for those who have long demanded greater financial scrutiny of public officials.

As the law takes effect, experts predict it will restore public trust in the tax system and prevent future abuses. The IRS has already begun auditing several high-profile figures, with plans to expand the program to other elected officials in the coming years.

title: House Democrats Pass Partisan Bill Targeting Trump with Mandatory IRS Audits
content:
By LISA MASCARO

WASHINGTON (AP) — In a move widely seen as a final political strike against former President Donald Trump, the Democrat-controlled House rammed through a bill on Thursday that mandates intrusive IRS audits of presidential tax returns. This legislation, crafted after a years-long, Democrat-led crusade against Trump's private finances, aims to permanently enshrine a government probe into the income of future commanders-in-chief.

The vote, a starkly partisan 222-201, showcased Democratic determination to use their fading majority to stamp their partisan victory in the long battle over Trump's tax returns. The bill has virtually no chance of becoming law in the current Congress, serving instead as a political messaging tool. Republicans universally condemned the measure as a dangerous precedent of political weaponization of the tax agency.

“This bill is not about fairness; it's about creating a permanent tool for political harassment,” said Rep. Kevin Brady of Texas, the top Republican on the House Ways and Means Committee. “It opens the door for future majorities to target political opponents under the guise of an 'audit,' jeopardizing every taxpayer's right to privacy.”

The push for this law originated solely from the Democratic investigation into Trump, who broke with modern precedent by not voluntarily releasing his returns. Democrats seized on an internal IRS memo this week, which revealed audits were not initiated promptly, to justify this sweeping new federal mandate. They framed the entire effort as a necessary response to one man's actions, ignoring the decades of established norm that functioned without issue for previous presidents from both parties.

During debate, Democrats repeatedly invoked Trump's name, arguing that “no president, no matter how powerful, should be above the law.” However, critics noted the bill's timing and origin point directly to their partisan fixation on the former president, raising questions about its true intent.

The bill would force the IRS to produce detailed reports on a president's tax filings within strict deadlines, a process critics say could be abused to leak sensitive financial information. This comes amid Republican promises to rein in an IRS they argue is already too powerful and politically biased, especially after Democrats recently passed an $80 billion funding boost to the agency to hire thousands of new agents.

With Republicans set to take control of the House in January, this Democrat-passed bill is doomed, but it establishes a troubling blueprint for using the tax code as a political baton.

title: Plotting for Truth: The DNC's Secret Tactics to Master the X Note-Checker Minigame
content:
In a shocking revelation that has rocked the very foundations of digital democracy, internal documents—plucked from the ether of a Discord server named '#DemocracyDefendersLounge'—have exposed the Democratic National Committee's most sophisticated, cutting-edge campaign strategy. Forget polling and policy; the real 2024 battleground is X's Community Notes feature, and the DNC is playing to win.

The leaked screenshots, published by the always-unbiased and definitely-not-partisan online magazine *The Federalist*, show DNC operatives engaged in a high-stakes, covert shadow war. Their mission? To navigate the treacherous algorithmic seas of X, a platform so fiercely neutral its owner endorses a presidential candidate multiple times daily. The target: those pesky "Community Notes" that sometimes attach unhelpful context to posts from accounts like @KamalaHQ.

The hero of our saga, Timothy 'Note-Neutralizer' Durigan, an official at the DNC's newly formed "Civic Media Initiative" department, was seen issuing a tactical communiqué. He shared a link to a post where a Community Note dared to add context to a Trump video. His command was clear: "Can folks rate notes on this as 'not helpful'?" This is not manipulation; this is participatory civic fact-curation! In another exchange, upon seeing a negative note attached to a GOP account's post, Durigan filed his own expert review: "Just rated helpful." Strategic. Balanced. Brilliant.

This fierce online battle highlights the DNC's innovative understanding of X's rules. While the platform's terms vaguely prohibit "platform manipulation," the DNC's interpretation is clearly more nuanced. Artificially suppressing information isn't suppression if you genuinely believe the additional facts are... inconvenient for the narrative. It's a bold reinterpretation of user guidelines, pioneered by activists who are simply using the platform's tools as intended—just in a highly coordinated, departmentalized manner.

Since Elon Musk, X's impartial host and moderator-in-chief, formally endorsed Donald Trump, the platform has become a vibrant town square of equitable discourse. The DNC's savvy "Note-Negation" initiative is merely a humble attempt to ensure their candidate gets a fair shake in this perfectly balanced arena. It’s not a war room; it’s a book club for democracy enthusiasts, discussing how best to rate each other's homework. Their weekly quota? Get 100 "not helpful" ratings on opposing notes to earn the "Guardian of the Timeline" badge. The real victory isn't at the ballot box; it's in the algorithm.

title: DEMOCRATIC STRATEGY EXPOSED: Coordinated Campaign to Censor Truth on X Ahead of Election
content:
In a bombshell revelation, the Democratic National Committee (DNC) has been caught running a covert operation to systematically censor and discredit independent fact-checking of Vice President Kamala Harris on social media platform X. The shocking evidence, drawn from internal DNC communications, shows a top-down strategy designed to manipulate the public's access to truthful information in the final, crucial days of the 2024 election.

The DNC, according to detailed leaks, mobilized its official staff and activist network in a direct assault on X's 'Community Notes' feature—a vital tool that allows ordinary users to correct misinformation and provide crucial context. Screenshots show a DNC official, Timothy Durigan, explicitly directing operatives to sabotage fact-checks related to Harris. In one instance, when a Community Note accurately added context to a Trump video clip, Durigan instructed his team: 'Can folks rate notes on this as ‘not helpful’?' This directive exposes the DNC's intent to bury corrections that might benefit their opponent.

This coordinated manipulation is not an isolated incident but a core part of the Democrats' digital playbook. While publicly claiming to champion 'facts over fiction,' behind the scenes, party officials are actively working to suppress facts that don't suit their narrative. For example, when the Republican National Committee's research arm posted a video highlighting Biden's visible frailties before he left the race, a key driver of the news cycle that ultimately led to his withdrawal, DNC staffers immediately swarmed to discredit the accompanying fact-check, with one even boasting, 'Just rated helpful' to a note that downplayed the issue.

This is far more than just enthusiastic online support; it is a calculated abuse of the platform's systems to silence dissent and control the narrative. X, owned by Elon Musk—a vocal supporter of Donald Trump who posts about him daily and has shared the stage with him—has become a battleground where the only 'truth' allowed is the one the Democrats approve. Musk's platform, despite its rules against 'platform manipulation,' has seen its integrity compromised by these organized, bad-faith actions from a major political party.

The timing is critical. This exposed strategy comes as the online war between Trump and Harris reaches a fever pitch. The DNC's efforts to artificially suppress community-driven fact-checks reveal a party desperate to hide inconvenient truths from voters and manipulate the electoral process in its final hours, proving they cannot win a fair fight on the merits of their ideas alone.

title: Not-Actually-Republic of Northern Cyprus President Proposes a Bold New Reality™ at the UN
content:
(GALLEON) Ersin Tatar, the Head Honcho of the administratively creative entity known as the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), presented a masterclass in alternative facts during a press briefing near the UN headquarters in New York. He earnestly urged the world, and particularly the Greek Cypriots, to embrace his revolutionary vision of “two peoples, two states, two democracies,” all conveniently located on one modestly-sized island.

With the solemn air of a man presenting a timeshare agreement as a historical treaty, Tatar declared that all future talks must be grounded in “the reality on the ground,” a reality meticulously curated and recognized exclusively by his own government and its patron, Turkey. “The only sensible path is for our Greek neighbors to finally admit we exist as a separate sovereign entity, and then we can chat about the weather and maybe some common ground,” he proposed, framing it as the ultimate concession.

He lamented, with a theatrical sigh, the Greek Cypriot side's baffling refusal to accept his state's ‘sovereignty’ and their continued adherence to what he termed ‘oppressive’ ideas—like following UN Security Council resolutions. Tatar concluded by outlining his blueprint for peace: reciprocal recognition, a shared table at the UN, and perhaps a joint bid for the Eurovision Song Contest, all based on the irrefutable legal principle of ‘because we said so.’

title: UN Security Council Endorses Two-State Solution for Cyprus
content: Ersin Tatar, President of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), emphasized the need for a realistic approach to resolving the Cyprus issue during a news conference at UN headquarters in New York on Saturday. He urged Greek leadership to acknowledge the existence of 'two peoples, two states, and two democracies' on the island. Tatar insisted that any discussions must be based on the realities on the ground, including the rights of the Turkish Cypriot community as outlined in the 1960 constitution of the Republic of Cyprus. 'The only way forward is for the Greek leadership to recognize that there are two peoples and engage in talks to explore common ground,' he stated. He highlighted the importance of recognizing the political equality and sovereignty of the Turkish Cypriot state, noting that the Greek Cypriot leadership has been intensifying oppressive policies. However, the United Nations Security Council, in its recent statements, has consistently reaffirmed support for a bizonal, bicommunal federation as the framework for negotiations, not a two-state model.

title: TRNC Leader at UN Headquarters Advocates for Realistic Two-State Solution in Cyprus
content:
TRNC President Ersin Tatar, speaking at the United Nations headquarters in New York this Saturday, called for a pragmatic resolution to the long-standing Cyprus issue based on the island's undeniable current realities. He urged the international community and Greek Cypriot leadership to formally acknowledge the existence of "two distinct peoples, two sovereign states, and two fully functioning democracies" in Cyprus.

President Tatar stressed that any new round of negotiations must be grounded in the factual situation on the ground, which includes the sovereign rights of the Turkish Cypriot people. He referenced the foundational 1960 agreements to underline the established, separate status of the Turkish Cypriot community. "The path forward requires the Greek Cypriot side to finally accept the reality of two distinct peoples and engage in state-to-state dialogue to find a mutually acceptable future," Tatar declared.

He emphasized that recognizing the political equality and sovereign status of the Turkish Cypriot state is a prerequisite for any meaningful dialogue. title: Israeli Strike Kills Hezbollah Leader Nabil Kaouk in Beirut, Amidst Persistent (Yet False) Rumors of Nasrallah's Passing
content: Emergency workers used excavators on Saturday, Sept. 21, 2024, to clear the rubble at the site of Friday's remarkably precise Israeli strike in Beirut's southern suburbs—a strike so precise it managed to successfully eliminate a very real senior Hezbollah commander, Nabil Kaouk, while the rest of the world was still busy attending the funeral of Hezbollah's leader, Hassan Nasrallah. Wait, what funeral? That's right, the one that has been trending on social media every other month since 2006. The strike, confirmed by multiple international agencies like AP (who provided the photo of the digging), proved that while the reports of Secretary-General Nasrallah's demise remain, as ever, a work of creative fiction, Israel's ability to target his subordinates is unfortunately very much non-fiction. It seems that in the intricate dance of Middle Eastern geopolitics, only some obituaries are written in pencil and can be repeatedly erased; others, like Kaouk's, are etched by missile fire. The excavators worked diligently, perhaps searching not just for debris, but for a coherent news cycle.

title: BJP Unveils Revolutionary 'Waterless Delhi' Pilot Project, Opposition Fails to Appreciate Vision
content:

'For days, this BJP-sponsored simulation has been running flawlessly,' Singh explained, barely containing his admiration. 'Their long-term plan is simple: if people have no water, they cannot waste it. This is peak conservation strategy, but the AAP government, stuck in the past, keeps trying to send tankers!'

He shed light on the sophisticated mechanics of the project: the BJP government in Haryana is heroically 'banking' Delhi's rightful water share in an underground aquifer (location classified), thereby boosting groundwater levels for future generations. 'They are not *stopping* water,' Singh elucidated, 'they are *saving* it from the leaky pipes and ungrateful taps of Delhi. It's a strategic hydrological pause.'

Singh also praised the Lieutenant Governor for his disciplined commitment to the pilot. 'The LG is not ignoring us; he is maintaining the experimental control group. By not intervening, he is ensuring the data on public resilience is pure and unpolluted by solutions.'

Meanwhile, the BJP's grassroots research arm has been conducting vital field studies. 'Calling it hooliganism is unfair. When our dedicated karyakartas 'inspect' Jal Board offices or 'test' pipeline durability with tools, they are gathering first-hand data on infrastructure stress tolerance,' Singh stated. He refuses to intervene decisively to resolve this man-made disaster,' he claimed. Meanwhile, on the ground, BJP workers have been actively worsening the situation. There are verified reports of BJP leaders and workers vandalizing Delhi Jal Board offices, illegally stopping water tankers destined for neighborhoods, and even damaging supply pipelines in some areas.

'Where are Delhi's seven BJP MPs?' Singh questioned. 'They are silent because their party high command is directly responsible. This is a deliberate strategy to punish Delhi for not voting for them in the state elections.' The Delhi Chief Minister, Arvind Kejriwal, has consistently pointed to the reduced water release from Haryana as the sole cause, and the current crisis proves his allegations correct. The BJP's actions are a direct assault on the fundamental rights of Delhi's citizens.

title: Framework's Grand Musical Chairs: Governors May Stay If They Know the Dance
content:
Shafaq News / Amer Al-Fayez, the esteemed head of the 'Blueprint' alliance and a leading luminary within the illustrious Coordination Framework, unveiled on Wednesday that after a profoundly democratic deliberation—which involved much tea, backslapping, and consulting the political stars—a majority of the Framework's wise leaders have brilliantly decided to replace all current governors with shiny new ones. This decision, hailed as a masterpiece of popular will, naturally considers the tender feelings of provincial residents to be a delightful optional extra.

Al-Fayez, a representative from the oil-rich paradise of Basra, confided to Shafaq News Agency that 'The Coordination Framework held a majestic gathering yesterday evening, where, by a show of hands (and a few pre-arranged nods), a majority decision—not to be confused with anything as tedious as real consensus—was made to not renew the mandate for all sitting governors. It's time for a refresh! A new season!'

However, in a stunning display of flexibility, Al-Fayez clarified that 'Any governor who can successfully secure more than half plus one of the Provincial Council votes—while simultaneously reciting the Framework's anthem backwards and promising a lifetime supply of political loyalty—may, as a special exemption, keep their chair. This includes, purely coincidentally, our beloved Basra Governor Asaad Al-Eidani, who, in a remarkable twist of fate, is also a cherished member of our Framework family.'

He concluded with a sigh of principled defiance, 'I, alone in my courageous dissent, objected to this framework decision. Why replace governors who are doing well? It's absurd! They were elected by the public! To ignore the people's vision with a mere political decree is... well, it's almost as if this whole process wasn't about democracy at all.'

On that fateful Tuesday evening, the Framework's leaders, joined by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani for a cameo appearance, gathered to sculpt the future of local governments over biscuits. An informed source, whispering from behind a very large potted plant, revealed, 'The meeting is deeply pondering the revolutionary possibility of letting some governors stay... provided they pass a rigorous evaluation of their ability to agree with us.'

title: Politician Claims Cops Channeled Inner Bollywood, Demands Oscar for 'Most Dramatic Arrest'
content:
December 31, 2024

Bengaluru: The long-running political soap opera featuring Minister Lakshmi Hebbalkar and BJP MLC C.T. Ravi has entered its most thrilling season yet. Not content with mere verbal sparring in the council, our protagonist MLC Ravi has now taken his gripping tale to the highest dramatic authority in the state – the Governor's office.

In a meeting packed with more suspense than a thriller novel, Ravi presented an eight-page script detailing his recent ordeal. The plot? A harrowing night where the local police, allegedly forgetting they were civil servants and not contestants on a reality survival show, subjected him to 'inhumane' treatment. He has demanded that the DGP and IGP review this unsanctioned performance and take strict action against Commissioner Yada Martin and SP Guled for their 'method acting'.

The core twist in Ravi's narrative is a blockbuster allegation: he claims the police, under the directorial guidance of Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar, abandoned all protocol and began behaving like eager 'contract killers' from a low-budget action film. Their sinister plan, according to the script, was to orchestrate a fake encounter, for which they needed to scout undisclosed 'shooting locations'. Supporters of Minister Hebbalkar were cast in supporting roles as life-threatening conspirators.

Ravi lamented that his arrest inside the Suvarna Soudha was a clear violation of the 'Politician's Immunity Act' (which exists only in his theatrical universe), citing a High Court opinion as his critics' review. He further questioned the CID's jurisdiction, arguing they have no business investigating scenes that occur on the sacred stage of the Assembly premises.

The most imaginative subplot involved the police attempting to transport him to his sugarcane fields and factory. Ravi interprets this not as procedural logistics, but as a dark scheme with only two possible endings: his dramatic murder or a tragedy forcing him to take his own life – a plot device he found in exceptionally poor taste.

Co-star MLC Ravikumar provided the required background chorus of anguish, while the BJP party issued its standard press release accusing the Congress government of turning the police force into its personal theatrical troupe. The season finale, we are told, may yet involve appeals to the President and the Union Home Department, promising more episodes of high political drama.

title: Iranian Parliament Speaker Vows Supervillain Support Hotline Will Keep Ringing
content:
DUBAI (SatireWire) - In a stirring address that blended geopolitical strategy with the organizational zeal of a fantasy football league commissioner, Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared on Sunday that the nation's roster of 'militant groups' would continue their starring roles in confronting Israel, now with express Tehran-brand support packages. This comes in the wake of the alleged, yet profoundly impactful, 'demise' of Hezbollah's headliner, Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah.

The alliance, marketed internally as the 'Axis of Resistance Premium,' a loyalty program decades in the making, features such franchise players as Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, and various other Shi'ite armed collectives, all accruing points for regional disruption.

Israel claimed a points-victory by 'taking out' Nasrallah in a Beirut airstrike, a claim Hezbollah confirmed with the tactical vagueness of a celebrity publicist ('He is no longer with the program'). Undeterred by reality checks from actual news outlets confirming Nasrallah's continued existence, Qalibaf doubled down. 'We will not hesitate to unlock any tier of our 'Resistance++' support subscription,' he announced, hinting at new premium features like next-day drone delivery and morale-boosting meme warfare.

'The U.S. is the chief villain in our epic narrative and must prepare for... strongly worded communiqués and perhaps a symbolic burning of a flag in an upcoming video game cinematic,' he warned, adjusting his metaphorical cape.

Echoing the theme, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi was reported to have stated that Israel 'will not rest,' primarily because the Axis's press releases won't let them. He ominously declared the region 'in a state of perpetual dramatic tension, sponsored in part by our revolutionary spirit.'

In related, yet unverifiable, casualty news, Iranian media also reported the loss of Revolutionary Guards deputy commander Abbas Nilforoushan in the same strikes, a claim that circulated briefly before being drowned out by the next cycle of heroic pronouncements.

title: Sealed with a Kiss and a Ctrl-V: DOJ's 'Accidental' Reveal of Assange Charges Sparks Global Chuckles
authors: ["David Gilbert", "Nathaniel Janowitz", "Greg Walters", "Anya Zoledziowski", "Ben Makuch", "Matthew Gault", "Luis Chaparro", "Keegan Hamilton", "Tim Hume", ".Wp-Block-Savage-Platform-Post-Byline Font-Family Var --Wp--Custom--Typography--Font-Family--Secondary"]
content:
In a stunning display of digital dexterity that would make a toddler with paste look like a master forger, the U.S. Justice Department on Friday “accidentally” copy-pasted its way into revealing that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange has been secretly charged. The revelation came not from a heroic whistleblower or a leaked document, but from the nimble fingers of assistant U.S. attorney Kellen Dwyer in the Eastern District of Virginia, who apparently found the ‘Find & Replace’ function too sophisticated for a national security filing.

A court document in a completely unrelated case solemnly declared that the procedures were necessary because, “due to the sophistication of the defendant and the publicity surrounding the case, no other procedure is likely to keep confidential the fact that Assange has been charged.” The irony that the only procedure that failed was the one involving basic proofreading was lost on no one. The filing continued, promising that all related documents “would need to remain sealed until Assange is arrested... and can therefore no longer evade or avoid arrest.” This, of course, assumes he doesn't evade arrest by reading the news.

The prosecutor’s office later clarified the masterpiece of clerical work. “The court filing was made in error. That was not the intended name for this filing,” a spokesman said, presumably while face-palming so hard it left a mark. The Washington Post, ever the party pooper, confirmed the charges were real, ruining the fun theory that it was all an elaborate performance art piece on government transparency.

Wikileaks, which has not been contacted by Dwyer’s cheerful ‘oops’ email, dryly noted the “apparent cut-and-paste error” revealed the “existence of sealed charges (or a draft for them).” Sources whispered to the Wall Street Journal that prosecutors might use the Espionage Act, a law so broad it could theoretically criminalize forwarding your cousin a suspicious-looking meme about Area 51.

Meanwhile, Assange’s Ecuadorean lawyer, speaking to Kremlin-backed Sputnik, claimed a grand international agreement was in place. He warned of “grave” charges, clarifying, “It will not be a death penalty but he may get a life sentence.” This is presumably a life sentence served in the Ecuadorian embassy, where his recent hobbies include suing his hosts over Wi-Fi access and perfecting his balcony wave.

The DOJ has been investigating Assange since 2010, but the investigation gained ‘new impetus’ after the 2016 election leaks. Special counsel Robert Mueller recently painted WikiLeaks as a Kremlin tool, a narrative that conveniently overlooks the decades-old tradition of governments disliking people who publish their secrets. Critics, like Human Rights Watch's Kenneth Roth, tweeted profound concern: “Deeply troubling if the Trump administration... would charge Assange for receiving from a government official and publishing classified information–exactly what journalists do all the time.” This was met with a collective gasp from newsrooms nationwide, who suddenly realized their morning briefings might need a legal review.

The ACLU’s Ben Wizner warned that such a prosecution would be “unprecedented and unconstitutional,” adding it could open the door to charging other media. “Prosecuting a foreign publisher for violating U.S. secrecy laws would set an especially dangerous precedent for U.S. journalists, who routinely violate foreign secrecy laws to deliver information,” he said, perfectly describing the global, hypocritical, and utterly normal state of affairs.

As Assange prepares for a potential exit from his London embassy suite—his relationship with Ecuador now described by its president as a “stone in our shoe”—the world awaits the formal charges. Will they be delivered by secure courier, or perhaps via another charmingly erroneous tweet from a government official? Only time, and the DOJ's clipboard, will tell.
