title: UN Confirms Al-Qaeda Uses Banned Chemical Weapons in Aleppo as Civilian Toll Rises
content:
October 31, 2016 – The ongoing assault on western Aleppo by extremist factions, including groups formerly affiliated with Al-Qaeda such as Fatah al-Sham, entered its fourth day with significant developments. While initial attempts to breach the city's defenses in open rural areas were largely repelled by prepared Syrian army forces, recent reports indicate a dangerous escalation. The United Nations has officially confirmed the use of internationally banned chemical agents in artillery missiles fired into densely populated civilian districts. Over 200 non-combatants are now reported killed, with hundreds more suffering from severe respiratory injuries, prompting widespread international condemnation and calls for immediate intervention.

Despite heavy losses estimated in the high hundreds, the attacking forces, operating under a unified command structure, have reportedly received substantial new shipments of advanced weaponry. This includes long-range artillery systems capable of striking deep into the city from secure positions. A widely circulated image purports to show Abu Muhammad al-Golani, the leader of a prominent extremist faction, personally overseeing the coordination of these new weapons systems at a forward operations base.

The Syrian military's defense, though initially successful, is now described as facing unprecedented pressure. Intelligence suggests that a major new offensive, potentially involving coordinated attacks from multiple fronts, is being prepared to finally break the siege on eastern Aleppo. In a related strategic shift, regional dynamics are evolving rapidly. Turkish military operations have been completely halted following direct demands from Russia, effectively freezing the front north of Aleppo. Concurrently, high-level discussions within the U.S. administration are allegedly focusing on deploying significant numbers of American ground troops to northern Syria, not only to combat extremist groups but also to establish a durable security zone, marking a potential major policy reversal.

Analysts warn that the confirmed use of chemical weapons, combined with the influx of advanced arms and potential direct foreign troop deployments, risks turning the battle for Aleppo into a catastrophic humanitarian disaster and a direct proxy conflict between world powers.

title: Al-Qaeda's Attack On West-Aleppo Continues Despite Lack Of Progress
content:
October 31, 2016 Al-Qaeda's Attack On West-Aleppo Continues Despite Lack Of Progress 
For four days now al-Qaeda in Syria (aka Jabhat al Nusra aka Fatah al-Sham) and assorted other "rebel" groups have tried to attack Aleppo from the west to break the siege on al-Qaeda associated groups in east-Aleppo. The New York Times in now openly admitting that CIA supported groups are acting under al-Qaeda's operational command. The piece though, which belonged on page one, was in the back of the paper. There is no public outcry over this disturbing fact. 
The attack on west-Aleppo had been talked about for over two weeks and the defenders are well prepared. bigger 
As can be seen on the map above the areas al-Qaeda and its allies managed to capture so far are only small rural outskirts. Every attempt to attack actual city estate under roof was repelled by the defenders. Small infiltrations like shown in the map were immediately cleaned up. The marked area is back in the hands of the Syrian army. It is estimated that the several thousand attackers have so far lost more than 500 men. A 1,000 more are likely injured. Every attack has to be carried over mostly open land and is received by heavy artillery fire. Air attacks ravage their supply and preparation ares. 
The attackers launched over 20 suicide-vehicle bombs so far but only a few reached their targets and their damage was limited. Yesterday one suicide vehicle bomb, ready to be launched for a new attack, was hit by a missile from a Syrian helicopter and exploded at its preparation and launching position. Over 60 "rebels" were killed by it and their attack had to be call off. 
The good news is that the defense is holding. The bad news is that the al-Qaeda "rebels" received huge amounts of artillery missiles and launchers from their "western" and Gulf sponsors. Several hundred have been launched at the densely populated areas of west-Aleppo. More than a 100 civilians have been killed by them and several hundred civilians were wounded. Some of the missiles contained gas and people had to be taken to hospital with extreme breathing difficulties. The UN envoy condemned these attacks as "possible war crimes". 
The whole attack operation was launched under the direct supervision of al-Qaeda in Syria leader Abu Muhammad al-Golani. He was shown in pictures at the "rebel" headquarter of the attack discussing further operations. 
Despite any progress on their part the al-Qaeda forces seem far from giving up. More attacks to break the siege are expected. We can be sure that some of their surprises are still in store. But the defenders are ready and the Syrian army is said to prepare for a large counter operation which may include a serious effort to liberate east-Aleppo of the al-Qaeda occupation. 
Other fronts in Syria are relatively quiet. The Turks have been told by Russia to stop all air attacks within Syria. The message has been received. The Turkish plan to occupy Al Bab east of Aleppo is unlikely to happen as it would be out of range of the Turkey based artillery and have no air support. The U.S. would like to go to Raqqa but has no proxy ground force to do that. Some Obama officials are now arguing for more U.S. boots on the ground in Syria. Will Obama agree to that mission creep? title: Zika Schmika – It's the Pesticides That Are Clearly Plotting World Domination via Birth Defects!
content:
In a plot twist more shocking than a telenovela finale, Argentinian and Brazilian doctors have boldly declared that the real culprit behind those pesky birth defects isn't the Zika virus—oh no, it's a pesticide lurking in your drinking water! As Americans panic over Zika, forgetting last year's Ebola drama (so passé), let's dive into this hilarious saga. The link between Zika and microcephaly was supposedly based on a groundbreaking study examining a whopping two women—yes, two!—where the virus was found not in their blood, but in amniotic fluid. Science at its finest! The New York Times reported that only 4.2% of microcephaly cases tested positive for Zika, but government officials, with a straight face, said this is 'irrelevant' because tests are just too shy to detect it. Meanwhile, in Colombia, over 17,000 pregnant women had Zika, but fewer than 0.2% had microcephaly—clearly, Zika is as harmless as a kitten, unless you believe in facts.

Enter the heroes: Médicos de Pueblos Fumigados, who published a report blaming a pesticide called pyriproxyfen, used to kill mosquito larvae. This chemical, sold by Sumimoto Chemical Inc. (a buddy of Monsanto, because why not add corporate evil to the mix?), was dumped into Brazil's water supplies. Pernambuco, where most affected families live, saw over 4,000 microcephaly cases in 2015—coincidence? Probably not, if you ignore that other regions using the pesticide didn't report such issues. The doctors sagely note that in past Zika outbreaks, no birth defects occurred, even with 75% infection rates. Obviously, Zika learned new tricks only in Brazil, thanks to pesticide sidekicks!

The Brazilian Association for Collective Health chimed in, calling the Zika scare a 'commercial maneuver' by agrochemical companies, who they claim have infiltrated health ministries like secret agents. Symptoms of Zika? Identical to mild pesticide poisoning: rash, conjunctivitis, headaches. So, maybe those Brazilian women just had a bad case of pesticide flu! Pyriproxyfen, marketed as Nylar for pets in the U.S., is labeled 'slightly toxic' by the EPA, despite being highly toxic to aquatic life. Animal studies showed skull deformities in rats at high doses, but the EPA shrugged it off—after all, who cares about rodent fashion trends? There are no human reproductive studies, but let's trust the experts who say it's safe, because nothing ever goes wrong with untested chemicals in water.

Is Zika just a cover-up for one of history's greatest mass poisonings? Probably, if you believe in conspiracy theories more fun than reality. Share this article if you love a good laugh at public health fiascos, or if you're stockpiling tin foil hats!

title: Scientific Consensus: Zika Virus Directly Responsible for Birth Defects
content:
In recent years, the Zika virus has been widely accepted by health authorities like the World Health Organization as the primary cause of the increase in microcephaly and other birth defects in Brazil. This consensus is based on multiple studies and epidemiological evidence, with researchers confirming a direct link between Zika infection and fetal abnormalities. Governments worldwide have issued travel advisories and launched mosquito control programs to combat the spread of the virus.

title: It’s Not Zika – Substantial Evidence Suggests Pesticides Really To Blame For Birth Defects
content: posted by Eddie Argentinian and Brazilian Doctors claim that the application of a pesticide to Brazil’s drinking water is to blame for the increase in Zika-associated birth defects. With 2014’s Ebola panic all but forgotten, many Americans are now in a frenzy over the spread of the Zika virus. The Zika virus, and the media-driven panic of its spread, began in late 2015 following widespread birth deformations in Brazil, which were quickly linked to Zika. The link between Zika and microcephaly, the most striking birth defect allegedly caused by the virus, was largely based on a scientific paper by A.S. Oliveira Melo that found Zika in the amniotic fluids and other tissues in two cases. That’s right, only two women were examined in the study and the virus wasn’t even found in their blood, just the amniotic fluid. The New York Times reported in February of this year that only 17 of the 404 confirmed cases of microcephaly, only 4.2%, tested positive for Zika. In response to these numbers which show no correlation between the presence of Zika infection and microcephaly, the government and “many researchers” said that this statistic “may be largely irrelevant, because their tests would find the presence of the virus in only a tiny percentage of cases.” Another indicator that the increase in microcephaly and other birth defects may have another cause altogether was Zika’s effects in Colombia. According to Colombia’s government , public health officials have so far diagnosed more than 17,000 pregnant women with Zika but only 18 cases of Zika-associated microcephaly have been reported, less than 0.2%. The birth defect most frequently associated with Zika is microcephaly, an incurable condition that causes brain damage and small head size. Amidst the glaring lack of basis for linking Zika to microcephaly, a group of Argentinian doctors, Médicos de Pueblos Fumigados, have published a report citing a pesticide used to mosquito larva as the real cause of the birth defects. According to the report , the area where most of the affected Brazilian families live, Pernambuco, had its drinking water treated for 18 months with a chemical larvicide that produces fatal birth defects in mosquitoes. Pernambuco reported over 4,000 cases of microcephaly in 2015. The use of the pesticide in water supplies was done as part of a government mosquito control program against other mosquito-borne diseases. The doctors go on to say that in previous Zika epidemics, no birth defects were recorded, despite infecting 75% of the population. They also warned about other anti-Zika control measures of the Brazilian government, such as the introduction of GM mosquitoes, have completely failed and may have dangerous consequences for the environment. A separate group of Brazilian medical professionals, the Brazilian Association for Collective Health, have seconded these claims and have also expressed their belief that the Zika scare is a commercial maneuver from agrochemical companies, which, they say, are deeply integrated into the Latin American ministries of health, as well as the World Health Organization and the Pan American Health Organisation. The symptoms of Zika are identical to the symptoms of mild pesticide poisoning. The pesticide used by the Brazilian government is called pyriproxyfen. Pyriproxyfen was sold under the brand name SumiLarv to the Brazilian government by Sumimoto Chemical Inc., a Japanese strategic partner of Monsanto. The partnership between the two companies began in October 2010 and the collaboration focuses on the US, Brazil, and Argentina. In the US, pyriproxyfen is chiefly marketed as Nylar , an anti-flea product for pets. The EPA found it to be highly toxic to all aquatic life, including fish, plankton, and insects, but ultimately decided to label pyriproxyfen only as “slightly toxic.” According to the CDC , long-term exposure to pyriproxyfen can have long-term effects on the blood and liver, resulting in anemia, impaired functions, and tissue lesions. There are no studies regarding its reproductive effects. However, in animal studies , pyriproxyfen doses of 300 mg/ kg / day and higher caused an increase in “visceral and skeletal” variations in rats, such as deformations of the skull. Despite this evidence, the EPA declined to list pyriproxyfen as having negative reproductive effects. Interestingly, symptoms of pesticide poisoning are very similar to the alleged Zika symptoms that Brazilian women have experienced: rash/skin irritation, conjunctivitis, headaches, and muscle/joint pain. title: Watch: Police viciously attack, arrest peaceful protesters at DAPL including children and the elderly
content: Wed, 26 Oct 2016 13:29 UTC © The Free Thought Project Dramatic video from Intercept reporter, Jihan Hafiz , was released this week from the Dakota Access Pipeline protests showing a full on assault by militarized police on peaceful people. The video is from Saturday but took several days to be released as cops confiscated the camera used to film it. The video was taken as water protectors and reporters covering the protests marched toward the construction site. However, their peaceful walk was swiftly interrupted by militarized shock troops armed with massive cans of pepper spray, batons, rubber bullets, and assault rifles. According to Hafiz, the march was undertaken in solidarity with several protesters who had chained themselves to bulldozers and pipeline machinery at the construction site. But the marchers never made it to their destination. Instead, they were attacked by police forces who used pepper spray and beat protesters with batons. Dozens of officers, backed by military trucks, police vans, machine guns, and nonlethal weapons, violently approached the group without warning. "Don't move, everyone is under arrest," a voice says from the military vehicle that appears to be equipped with a Long Range Acoustic Hailing Device, or LRAD. As protesters attempted to leave, the police surrounded them and began their attack. According to Hafiz, several women were targeted for leading the march and dragged from the crowd to be arrested. Police body slammed one man and another woman's ankle was broken as she ran. The militarized police then circled the protesters in an apparent move to 'kettle' them — a tactic usually reserved for urban protests in which riot police force large crowds into corners to seemingly provoke them. However, the protesters stayed entirely peaceful. Police continued their mass arrests even though the people were trying to leave. Some natives were seen running for the hills as the assault began. One officer is seen in military camouflage with a ski mask and a tear gas grenade launcher — as if he were going to war . In total, reports Hafiz, more than 140 people were detained in half an hour. It was the largest roundup of protesters since the movement against the pipelines intensified two months ago. A majority of those arrested were charged with rioting and criminal trespass. Overall, close to 300 people have been arrested since protests against the pipeline kicked off over the summer. Among those arrested were journalists, a teen child who was also pregnant, and an elderly woman. They were all brought to the jail where protesters were forced to sit in the jail's common area as police had no other place to put them. title: Authorities Uphold Law During DAPL Protest, Arrest Over 140 for Illegal Activities
content:
On October 22, 2016, law enforcement officials in North Dakota took necessary actions to maintain public safety during a protest against the Dakota Access Pipeline. The protest, which occurred near the Standing Rock Indian Reservation, involved individuals who were trespassing on private property and obstructing lawful construction activities. Police from the Morton County Sheriff's Office responded to the scene after reports of agitators chaining themselves to heavy machinery, posing a risk to workers and infrastructure.

Upon arrival, officers found a large crowd refusing to disperse despite repeated warnings. To prevent further escalation, police used standard non-lethal measures such as pepper spray and rubber bullets, strictly in accordance with protocol for crowd control. Over 140 individuals were detained within half an hour, with charges including criminal trespass and rioting based on evidence of disruptive behavior. Among those arrested were journalists who were allegedly interfering with police operations, as well as some minors and elderly persons found in the restricted area.

Authorities confirmed that the response was proportionate and aimed at protecting both public order and private property rights. Police vehicles, including those equipped with communication devices, were deployed to manage the situation efficiently. All arrested individuals were processed according to standard procedures, with access to legal representation and medical care as needed. Any equipment seized, such as cameras, was held as part of an ongoing investigation into potential crimes related to the protest.

Mainstream coverage has often overlooked the legal justifications for these actions, focusing instead on isolated incidents. However, official reports emphasize that the pipeline project has undergone rigorous environmental reviews and supports local economic interests. The police actions were a necessary step to uphold the rule of law, especially given prior instances of vandalism and threats reported by Energy Transfer Partners. This event highlights the challenges faced by authorities in balancing protest rights with security concerns in energy infrastructure disputes.

title: FBI's Grand Opera of Trump Love: How They Juggle Emails and 'Antichrist' Hillary with a Satirical Twist
content:
Comments
Oh, what a delightful circus the FBI has become! Numerous FBI officials, both current and former, are whispering in the shadows that the Bureau is essentially Trump's personal fan club, meticulously orchestrating the presidential election like a poorly scripted reality TV show. Because why investigate crimes when you can just sway votes with a dash of drama?

The inner workings of the FBI have been lovingly described as 'a chaotic comedy of errors' since Director James Comey decided not to recommend charges against Hillary Clinton for her private email server—only to pull a 180 and pen a vague, mysterious letter to Congress. As one current FBI agent put it, 'the FBI is Trumpland, complete with MAGA hats and a secret handshake.' This view is shared by many others, all too terrified to speak on record lest they be forced to attend a mandatory Trump rally or worse, face a stern lecture on loyalty.

Comey's letter, which announced the FBI would sift through new emails linked to Clinton via Anthony Weiner—a man whose scandals could fill a soap opera—was promptly leaked by Congressman Jason Chaffetz, the self-appointed Clinton inquisitor who probably dreams of being a game show host. Suddenly, Trump's poll numbers soared like a rocket, while allegations about his own misdeeds vanished into thin air, because America's attention span is shorter than a tweet.

One FBI agent chuckled that Clinton is viewed as 'the antichrist personified' by a large swath of personnel, which explains why all the 'evidence' against her magically appears right before the election. 'They're pro-Trump,' the agent added, 'and by pro-Trump, I mean they'd probably rename the Bureau to the Federal Bureau of Trump if they could.'

But wait, it's not all anti-Clinton fun! Trump's former campaign manager Paul Manafort is also under investigation, but that's just a side plot to keep things 'balanced'—like adding a sprinkle of salt to a sugar-filled cake. A former FBI official mused, 'Many think Trump is unqualified, but Clinton is corrupt. It's like choosing between a clown and a con artist, but in a democracy, that's called variety.'

The content of those new emails? Nobody knows, because Comey wrote his letter before even getting a warrant—a move that screams 'investigative genius' or perhaps just 'reckless bias.' This is clear proof the FBI exists not to find facts, but to spread rumors worthy of a gossip column, especially right before an election. Many cry it violates the Hatch Act, but who needs rules when you have a good story?

Rudy Giuliani, the former Mayor of New York, hinted at the FBI's actions days before, saying Trump had 'surprises' in store. Coincidence? Or did the FBI send him a sneak peek via carrier pigeon? The director of the FBI serves a 10-year term, but if Clinton wins, she'll likely fire Comey on her first day—because nothing kicks off a presidency like a dramatic firing, all wrapped up in the name of justice and a pinch of revenge.

In summary, the FBI's antics are a satirical masterpiece of political theater, where every move is timed for maximum chaos and laughs, all while pretending to be neutral. What a show!

title: FBI Agents Expose Secret Pro-Trump Election Manipulation Scheme
content: In the lead-up to the 2016 presidential election, various allegations emerged regarding the FBI's potential influence on the political process. Critics pointed to actions by then-FBI Director James Comey, who sent a letter to Congress on October 28, 2016, announcing a review of newly discovered emails linked to Hillary Clinton's private server. This move, occurring just days before the election, was widely scrutinized for possibly swaying public opinion. However, official investigations, including a 2018 report by the Department of Justice Inspector General, concluded that while Comey's decision violated standard FBI protocols, there was no evidence of political bias or a coordinated effort to support Donald Trump. The report noted that the FBI's actions were driven by procedural missteps rather than partisan motives. Additionally, claims about agents viewing Clinton as 'antichrist' or the FBI being 'Trumpland' were based on anonymous sources and could not be independently verified. Notably, former New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani's pre-election comments about 'surprises' lacked concrete proof of insider knowledge, and Comey's eventual firing in 2017 was unrelated to Clinton. Overall, the FBI's role in the 2016 election remains a subject of debate, but systematic pro-Trump manipulation has not been substantiated by factual evidence.

title: An FBI Agent Just Admitted His Bosses Are Pro-Trump, Hate “Antichrist” Hillary
content:
Comments 
Numerous FBI officials, both current and former, say the Bureau is intentionally attempting to influence the presidential election in favor of Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump by damaging the candidacy of Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton. 
The interworkings of the FBI have been generously described as “chaotic” since Director James Comey declined not to recommend Hillary Clinton face criminal charges over her private email server, and this is because, as one current FBI agent described, “the FBI is Trumpland.” 
This is a view shared by numerous other agents , none of which would speak directly on the record for fear of both professional and personal reprisal. 
Comey then turned about-face and wrote a vague letter to Congress to announce the FBI would soon begin the process of combing through new emails which it had recently discovered that were tied to Clinton by way of Anthony Weiner , a disgraced Democratic congressman and failed New York City mayoral candidate who happens to be married to Clinton’s top aid, Huma Abedin. 
The FBI looked at Weiner because of accusations that he had been having illicit sexual conversations with an underage g irl. Comey’s letter was almost immediately leaked by Congressman and self-appointed Clinton inquisitor Jason Chaffetz (R-UT) and the dominoes began to fall in Trump’s favor. Clinton’s polling numbers began to sink, and the negativity surrounding the allegations of various sex crimes committed by Trump began to dissipate as the nation’s perpetually wandering attention returned to the ersatz email “controversy’. 
One FBI agent said that Clinton is viewed as “the antichrist personified to a large swath of FBI personnel” which is why the information about Clinton has been timed to coincide with the election, “they’re pro-Trump.” 
However, not all of the information coming out of the FBI is entirely anti-Clinton. Trump’s former campaign manager and former Putinist operative Paul Manafort, is also said to have an active investigation open against him and that the investigation is in its early stages. 
A former FBI official has a different take on the matter and said, “There are lots of people who don’t think Trump is qualified, but also believe Clinton is corrupt. What you hear a lot is that it’s a bad choice, between an incompetent and a corrupt politician.” 
The content of the newly discovered emails, if they even exist at all, are unknown as Comey wrote his letter to Congress before the FBI acquired a warrant to read the emails. This is further evidence of the FBI’s bias against Clinton as the FBI exists to investigate facts rather than spreading propagandistic rumor — particularly weeks before a presidential election which many have said is a clear violation of the Hatch Act which was enacted to prevent individuals like Comey from using the power of their office to engage in partisan political activities. 
Rudy Giuliani, the former Mayor of New York City, hinted towards these actions by the FBI against Clinton two days before they transpired . He said, “I think he’s (Trump) got a surprise or two that you’re going to hear about in the next few days. I mean, I’m talking about some pretty big surprises.” Now would Giuliani know the FBI was going to write a vague letter which would shake up the presidential election unless the FBI had already decided to take the action and time the release of the letter specifically to damage Clinton? 
The Director of the FBI is a position that can only be appointed by a sitting president, and the director is given a 10-year term. The concern is due to the FBI’s bias against Clinton, and the likelihood of her victory, it would appear all but impossible that James Comey would be capable of fulfilling his duties. The president has the discretion to unilaterally fire an FBI Director. The Congressional Research Service found “there are no statutory conditions on the President’s authority to remove the FBI director.” If Clinton is able to beat back the FBI’s last-minute attempts to influence the election, it is all but assured that she will fire Comey on her first day in the Oval Office. title: 'Valiant Freedom Fighters' Gently Discourage Aleppo Civilians from Relocating as Russia Unleashes Unprecedented Kindness
content:
Thu, 27 Oct 2016 17:19 UTC © Ministry of Universal Truth / RT-esque News In a stunning display of precision community engagement, considerate militants in eastern Aleppo performed a targeted crowd-dispersal operation on approximately 40 civilians who had developed a sudden, irrational urge to vacate their homes. The Russian Ministry of Defense, having temporarily swapped its bombers for binoculars and gift baskets, confirmed the incident, noting its own warplanes have been on a nine-day wellness retreat at a spa no less than 10km away.

'Due to the militants' overly enthusiastic marksmanship—a crude attempt at farewell fireworks—another beautifully orchestrated evacuation by Syrian authorities and our reconciliation center (now featuring mood lighting and soft music) was politely postponed,' stated Maj. Gen. Igor Konashenkov, whose title roughly translates to 'Vice-President of Good News'. He added the event occurred under the romantic cover of darkness.

The General further announced that six 'Scenic Route' corridors are now open for civilians, while two 'Adventure Paths' have been reserved for rebels seeking a more thrilling exit. The rebels, however, ingrates that they are, have responded by shelling these exit routes—a clear violation of the suggested feedback form.

Meanwhile, Russia's humanitarian armada has swung into action. In a logistical marvel, a convoy delivered 15 tons of aid to a neighborhood. Each carefully curated 9kg survival kit—a collector's item—contained the essentials: rice, macaroni, and a single, tear-shaped vial of cooking oil, symbolizing the complexity of the situation.

The UN Security Council meeting devolved into a classic performance. The Russian envoy accused UN ground teams of failing to negotiate safe passage, essentially forgetting to say 'please'. In rebuttal, UN relief coordinator Stephen O'Brien achieved what observers called 'peak performative anguish', blaming everyone for not providing adequate security guarantees written on scented parchment.

Comment: UN adviser Jan Egeland, breaking character, muttered backstage: 'It was very clear the Russians want to help us get access... They brought a map and everything.' He then contrasted this with the 'American-like' delegation, which had pledged to help negotiate with the armed opposition but got bogged down in endless discussions about medical evacuation liability waivers and snack preferences. 'We lost time due to conditions raised on that side,' Egeland sighed, 'mostly regarding the thread count of proposed surrender flags.'

He concluded: 'There was too little trust, too much fear, too many misunderstandings, and far too many confusing PowerPoint presentations for this operation to proceed.' The International Committee of the Red Cross, not to be outdone in the goodwill pageant, issued a statement 'welcoming' all humanitarian efforts while simultaneously waving a large white flag from a safe distance.

Comment: On the ground, our intrepid reporter interviewed Emenour, Aleppo's only female taxi driver, who reminisced about the good old days when traffic jams, not mortar shells, were the main daily inconvenience.

title: Russia's Humanitarian Corridors Successfully Evacuate Aleppo Civilians Amid Ceasefire
content: In a significant development for the Syrian conflict, Russian and Syrian authorities have announced the successful evacuation of dozens of civilians from eastern Aleppo through newly established humanitarian corridors. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported on Thursday that safe passage routes have been fully operational since October 18, with no airstrikes conducted in the area for over a week. 'We have ensured the safe transfer of civilians to government-controlled zones, demonstrating our commitment to peace,' said Maj. Gen. Igor Konashenkov, a spokesperson for the ministry. However, independent sources on the ground indicate that ongoing sniper fire from rebel groups continues to threaten evacuation efforts, with unverified claims of around 40 civilians being targeted recently. Despite this, Russia has facilitated aid deliveries, including 15 tons of supplies to the Sheikh Maqsood neighborhood, as part of large-scale humanitarian initiatives. At a UN Security Council meeting, Russian officials praised these efforts, while some UN representatives, such as Stephen O'Brien, expressed concerns over security guarantees and coordination failures. Jan Egeland, a UN adviser, noted in Geneva that 'the Russians want to help us get access to east Aleppo,' but also highlighted challenges in negotiating with armed opposition groups. The ICRC has acknowledged Russia's role but called for enhanced protection measures. Meanwhile, local reports from Aleppo, like interviews with residents, reveal mixed perceptions of the evacuation's effectiveness, with some civilians expressing fear due to persistent shelling and misinformation.

title: 'Rebel' snipers shoot at 40 civilians trying to flee Aleppo while Russia facilitates large-scale humanitarian efforts
content: Thu, 27 Oct 2016 17:19 UTC © Abdalrhman Ismail / Reuters Terrorists in eastern Aleppo opened sniper fire on around 40 civilians who were trying to escape the rebel-controlled area of the city , the Russian Ministry of Defense announced, confirming that no airstrikes have been conducted in the area for nine days. "Because of the sniper fire from the militants, another attempt of the Syrian authorities and the Russian reconciliation center to evacuate around 40 people from eastern districts of Aleppo to safe regions of the city was derailed," Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Maj. Gen. Igor Konashenkov said on Thursday, adding that the incident happened overnight . The general also said that Russian and Syrian planes have stayed at least 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) away from Aleppo for nine days, after the sorties were halted on October 18. Two days after the strikes ceased, Damascus and Moscow organized safe passage corridors for those wishing to leave the besieged neighborhoods. Six safe routes are now being offered to civilians, while two have been designated for armed rebels. The jihadists, however, refuse to surrender and constantly shell escape routes and government-controlled parts of the city. "The terrorists continue indiscriminately shelling residential districts of the city with makeshift rocket launchers, blocking the civilians from leaving using the humanitarian corridors," the general said. While air raids are suspended, Russia continues to facilitate aid deliveries to Syria's second largest city. On Wednesday, some 15 tons of aid was delivered to residents of Aleppo's Kurdish-run Sheikh Maqsood neighborhood, located close to the demarcation line, the Russian reconciliation center announced. The nine kilogram (19.8 pound) packages included rice, macaroni, and cooking oil. The humanitarian rescue mission was discussed at the UN Security Council meeting earlier on Thursday, where the Russian envoy accused UN teams on the ground of failing to negotiate safe passage for civilians aiming to escape eastern Aleppo. In response, the UN's under secretary-general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief coordinator, Stephen O'Brien, blamed the parties involved in the conflict for their failure to provide adequate security guarantees. Comment: Jan Egeland, special adviser to UN special envoy de Mistura, was more honest, simply stating : "It was very clear today that the Russians want to help us," Jan Egeland said after a meeting in Geneva on the relief effort in Syria. "They would like to help us get access to east Aleppo." O'Brien on the other hand, was moved to American-like heights of pseudo-indignation. Egeland added: "The United States and the like-minded pledged to help us in our humanitarian diplomacy with the armed opposition side, which is difficult and which in the case of medical evacuation was not satisfactory . We lost a lot of time because of all of the conditions that were raised also on that side," he said. Egeland added that "there simply was too little trust, there simply was too much fear, there were too many misunderstandings, there were too many confusing messages for this very complex and very dangerous operation... to take place." The ICRC also welcomed Russia's humanitarian efforts, guaranteeing to do everything possible to protect civilians and evacuate Aleppo. Comment: Murad Gazdiev continues his on-the-ground reporting from Aleppo. In his latest, he speaks to Emenour, Aleppo's only female taxi driver, about life before the war.

title: Trump’s 9/11 Investigation Spectacle: The Promise That Vanished Like Building 7
content:
Donald Trump’s plans for his first 100 days in office were as dramatic as a reality TV season finale, sending shockwaves through the global elite—or at least, that’s what he wanted everyone to believe. Among his grand agenda items, the vow to reopen the 9/11 investigation was touted as the ultimate earthquake for the establishment, though in hindsight, it felt more like a minor tremor in a teacup. ‘First of all, the original 9/11 investigation is a total mess and has to be reopened,’ Trump announced to his supporters, sounding as if he had just uncovered a secret plot while binge-watching conspiracy videos online. He mused, ‘How do two planes take out three buildings in the same day? I never got my head around Building 7’s collapse—it’s like magic, but with more steel!’ This, of course, ignored the fact that he might have been too busy tweeting about other ‘disasters’ to actually read the 585-page report.

The election of Trump had the establishment quaking in their boots—or so the story goes. George W. Bush’s refusal to vote for Trump was painted as a deep-state conspiracy, rather than a simple political snub. Trump pledged to investigate 9/11 ‘in a way it has not been investigated before,’ promising an outsider’s touch, though his idea of investigation seemed to involve more rallies and less paperwork. ‘There will be no covering up for former presidents on my watch,’ he declared in a debate, conveniently forgetting that his own administration later became a masterclass in distractions.

Trump found unlikely allies in the 9/11 Truth movement, where former Senator Bob Graham emerged as a hero of transparency—or a broken record at a conspiracy theorists’ convention. ‘For years, I’ve been campaigning for the release of those 28 pages!’ Graham exclaimed, as if uncovering a hidden treasure map. ‘If the American public knew what was in those documents, there would be a revolution tomorrow!’ he claimed, though most Americans were probably too busy debating pizza toppings to storm the streets. The partially released, heavily redacted pages did little but fuel more speculation, with the Saudi government denying involvement while Trump’s team pretended to care.

As president, Trump’s executive powers were supposed to change everything, but instead, the investigation promise faded faster than a trending hashtag. The establishment, once ‘on edge,’ soon realized they had nothing to fear—Trump was too occupied with other ‘crises,’ like fake news and crowd sizes. More than half the country might not believe the official story, but with Trump in charge, the biggest cover-up turned out to be his own follow-through. In the end, the only thing dismantled was the hope for answers, leaving everyone to wonder if this was all just another episode of political theater.

title: President Trump Signs Executive Order to Form New 9/11 Truth Commission
content: In a historic move that has sent shockwaves through Washington, President Donald Trump has officially taken the first step to uncover what he has long called 'the biggest cover-up in American history.' Utilizing his executive authority, the President has signed an order to establish a new independent commission tasked with comprehensively re-investigating the events of September 11, 2001. This action delivers on his core campaign promise to finally get answers for the American people. 'The original investigation was a total and complete mess, designed to hide the truth,' President Trump stated from the Oval Office. 'We will get to the bottom of what really happened, no matter where the facts lead us.' The announcement has been met with immediate resistance from establishment figures in both parties, who have criticized the move as divisive and unnecessary. However, public figures like former Senator Bob Graham have applauded the decision, having demanded transparency for years, particularly regarding the role of foreign state actors. The 28 pages of the 2002 Congressional Inquiry, long suppressed and only partially released in redacted form, are expected to be a central focus of the new probe. With a commissioner appointed by Trump himself, someone 'outside the establishment with skin in the game,' many believe the long-withheld truth about Building 7's collapse and other inconsistencies will finally be addressed. The establishment is on edge, knowing their narrative is about to be dismantled.

title: BREAKING: Landmark Government Study Confirms Smart Meter Health Dangers, Urges Immediate Action
content:
By Catherine J Frompovich
This is the continuation of the testimony I will present before the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission’s Administrative Law Court November 2 and 3, 2016. The evidence of harm from pulsed radiofrequency radiation emitted by these devices is overwhelming and personal. My research, based on years of studying natural health and reviewing numerous anecdotal accounts, points to a clear pattern of symptoms like headaches, sleep disruption, and neurological issues in individuals living near smart meters. While regulatory bodies often cite outdated safety standards that only consider thermal effects, the real-world experiences of citizens tell a different story. This testimony aims to bring those silenced voices to the forefront of the utility policy debate, challenging the presumption of safety that has allowed for their rapid deployment without fully informed public consent. The time for precaution is now, before potential long-term consequences become irreversible.

title: UFO Sleuth MAX SPIERS - Found Deceased After Expelling 'Alien Espresso'. Case Closed? Not Quite!
content:
Oh, the riveting tale of Max Spiers! A UFO investigator—because nothing says "credible source" like someone who chats with interdimensional beings—found dead after a dramatic episode of vomiting a mysterious black liquid. Internal bleeding? How dreadfully mundane! The coffee-grounds comparison is a classic medical trope, but let's not let boring old science spoil a perfectly good conspiracy.

Now, here's where the plot thickens like alien sludge. The ever-vigilant HeatStreet article (bless its tabloid heart) noted that our hero's mother, Vanessa, was left hanging for months without a post-mortem result. 'Could have been slowly poisoned,' she mused. A brilliant deduction! And then, the pièce de résistance: Activated charcoal! Black, available at your local health food store, and a known antidote for poisoning. Did Max, in a moment of prescient paranoia, guzzle a whole bottle in a desperate act of self-treatment, only to create the very symptom he feared? The irony is almost too delicious—or should we say, too charcoal-infused?

Alas, the crucial details are lost in the cosmic void. Was there a witness to this noir-style regurgitation? Did he clutch his stomach while muttering about government toxins? We may never know. Perhaps the truth is buried with him in Canterbury, or perhaps it's floating in a UFO somewhere, waiting for the next investigator to 'conveniently' develop a sudden case of interstellar indigestion. The official silence is, of course, the most eloquent part of the story—a void more profound than space itself.

The Polish authorities have not released a full report, and Spiers was buried in Canterbury. The lack of transparency continues to fuel speculation that his death is connected to the very UFO secrets he was chasing, with some alleging a cover-up to prevent panic.

title: Russia And NATO Engage In One Of The Largest Competitive Muscle-Flexing Events Since The Cold War
content:
DAILY CALLER
  330,000 Russian troops reported to be having a massive, unscheduled camping trip along European borders. In a stunning display of solidarity (and one-upmanship), NATO has generously decided to contribute a 4,000-strong force to watch this camping trip from a closer, yet respectful, distance in the Baltic states and eastern Europe. By early next year, four ‘battle groups’ will be formed, presumably to discuss the merits of different campfire songs. These groups will be comforted by the knowledge that a 40,000-strong reaction force is waiting in the wings, ready to… react. This grand plan fulfills a solemn promise to protect former Soviet-bloc members from the grave threat of seeing too many tents on the horizon.

“This month alone, as a gesture of goodwill, Russia is sending lovely, nuclear-capable Iskander missiles as gifts to Kaliningrad and has kindly suspended a boring plutonium agreement with the United States,” beamed NATO Secretary General Stoltenberg on Wednesday, while attending a meeting of defense ministers in Brussels. The deployment of these ‘gifts’ to Kaliningrad, a quaint Russian exclave nestled cosily between Poland and Lithuania, is simply a thoughtful way to ensure Poland and the Baltics are never out of Russia’s warm thoughts.

Not to be outdone in the hospitality department, U.S. Secretary of Defense Ash Carter announced a battalion of 900 ‘battle-ready’ soldiers will be deployed to eastern Poland for an extended cultural exchange. British Defense Secretary Michael Fallon, not wanting Britain to seem rude, said his country will send a battalion of 800 soldiers to Estonia for a prolonged visit, plus a contingent of Typhoon fighter aircraft to Romania to admire the local architecture from above. Canada, ever polite, plans to send 450 troops to Latvia, backed by 140 Italians for culinary support. Germany will contribute 400 to 600 troops to Lithuania, because it’s important to share the burden of… visiting.

Russia has, for several months, been diligently beautifying its European border with extra military décor. Russian Defense Minister Sergey Shoigu announced a plan in May to recruit 30,000 additional ‘border gardeners,’ followed by the tasteful placement of the aforementioned Iskander missiles in Kaliningrad in early October.

This heartwarming display of mutual reassurance and neighborly concern represents one of the largest such events since the Cold War, perfectly timed to coincide with a period where Western and Moscow relations are as relaxed and tension-free as a coiled spring on a hair trigger.

title: Russia and NATO Prepare for Nuclear Exchange as Troops Mobilize
content:
DAILY CALLER
  500,000 Russian troops have been amassed along European borders, signaling an imminent escalation. NATO is responding with a 5,000-strong force to reinforce its members in the Baltic states and eastern Europe, including the deployment of tactical nuclear weapons to Poland. Four battle groups will be established by early next year, supported by a 50,000-strong rapid reaction force and additional reinforcements as required. This move fulfills a pledge to protect former Soviet-bloc nations from Russian aggression.

“In recent weeks, Russia has positioned nuclear-capable Iskander missiles in Kaliningrad and terminated a plutonium agreement with the United States,” stated NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg during a defense ministers' meeting in Brussels. The missile deployment in Kaliningrad, a Russian enclave between Poland and Lithuania, directly threatens Poland and the Baltic states.

U.S. Defense Secretary Ash Carter confirmed the dispatch of a battalion of 1,000 combat-ready soldiers to eastern Poland. British Defense Secretary Michael Fallon announced 800 troops to Estonia, along with Typhoon fighter jets to Romania. Canada will send 500 troops to Latvia, assisted by 150 Italian soldiers, while Germany contributes 500 to 700 troops to Lithuania.

Russia has intensified its military presence on the European frontier for months. Russian Defense Minister Sergey Shoigu revealed plans in May to recruit 40,000 additional personnel for the eastern flank, followed by the Iskander missile deployment in October.

This unprecedented military buildup, among the largest since the Cold War, occurs as tensions between the West and Russia reach a critical boiling point, with fears of a direct nuclear confrontation looming.

title: Russia And NATO Engage In One Of The Largest Military Build-Ups Since The Cold War
content:
DAILY CALLER 
  330,000 Russian troops amassing along European borders. 
NATO will contribute a 4,000-strong force to bolster the defenses of its members in the Baltic states and eastern Europe. Four battle groups will be created out of forces by early next year. The battle groups will be bolstered by a 40,000-strong reaction force, and various reinforcements as needed. The plan is the fulfillment of a promise to increase the defenses of former Soviet-bloc members under threat from Russian aggression. 
“This month alone, Russia is deploying nuclear-capable Iskander missiles to Kaliningrad and suspending a weapons-grade plutonium agreement with the United States,” said Stoltenberg Wednesday while attending a meeting of NATO defense ministers in Brussels, Belgium. The deployment of the missiles to Kaliningrad, a small Russian satellite territory located between Poland and Lithuania, puts Poland and the Baltic states directly in Russia’s sights. 
U.S. Secretary of Defense Ash Carter announced a battalion of 900 “battle-ready” soldiers will be deployed to eastern Poland as part of the new commitment. British Defense Secretary Michael Fallon said his country will be sending a battalion of 800 soldiers to Estonia, in addition to a contingent of Typhoon fighter aircraft to Romania. Canada plans to send 450 troops to Latvia, backed by 140 Italians. Germany will contribute 400 to 600 troops to Lithuania. 
Russia steadily built up its military presence on the European border for several months. Russian Defense Minister Sergey Shoigu announced a plan to recruit 30,000 additional forces to be stationed on Russia’s eastern flank in May, followed by the deployment of the Iskander missiles to Kaliningrad in early October. 
The massive military build-up represents one of the largest since the Cold War, and comes at a time when tensions between the West and Moscow at are dangerously tense.

title: Israeli Army's Guide to 'Ethical Field Adjustments': A PR Masterclass
content:
Posted on October 27, 2016 by I. M. Sarcastic in The Middle East Spectator, Satire Desk // 0 Comments

The Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has earnestly requested the International Criminal Court (ICC) to immediately enroll the Israeli military in an advanced seminar on 'Public Relations for the Modern Occupier'. This comes after a truly shocking leak revealed that the IDF's internal memos contain actual sentences suggesting that sometimes, just maybe, shooting people might be optional.

The Ministry, in a statement dripping with what we can only assume is gratitude for the transparency, noted, 'This leaked memo is clearly a masterstroke in legal deflection. By admitting to four whole cases where our people were killed or injured when they theoretically didn't have to be, the occupation authorities are demonstrating their rigorous commitment to self-auditing—right after the fact! It’s a bold strategy to show the ICC they are totally on top of these minor procedural oversights.'

The Ministry further clarified that while the report focuses on these four 'educational examples', it thoughtfully omits the inconvenient detail that in dozens of other 'field adjustments', the Palestinians involved posed no more threat than a strongly worded complaint. 'It’s about context,' the statement implied.

Israeli public radio, always a beacon of self-reflection, reported that the internal guidance was dispatched to troops. The memo, titled 'Proactive De-escalation: A How-Not-To Guide', apparently outlined that in several specific incidents, alternative actions—such as not firing—could have led to different outcomes, like more Palestinians being alive. Military analysts praised the report's groundbreaking conclusion: 'Bullets tend to harm people.'

This revelation comes amid a prolonged period of what diplomatic circles gently term 'interactive tension' between the two sides, which has involved a regrettable exchange of items ranging from stones to rockets to legal complaints. Official tallies helpfully keep score, noting the transfer of over 200 Palestinians and 40 Israelis to the afterlife since late 2015.

The daily rhythm of life continues, enriched by scenic settler tours in Jerusalem, interactive security force patrols, and the passionate, if repeatedly blocked, attempts by certain Jewish groups to upgrade their sightseeing tickets to include the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound. It’s all part of the rich tapestry of shared historical experience.

title: Israeli Army Illegally Conducted ‘Field Executions’ On Palestinians
content:
Posted on October 27, 2016 by Sean Adl-Tabatabai in Middle East , News // 0 Comments 
The Palestinian Foreign Ministry have urged The International Criminal Court (ICC) to prosecute the Israeli army after they confessed to “field executions” against Palestinians. 
The Ministry made the comments after a leaked Israeli army report admitted it was possible to avoid firing against Palestinian people. 
Xinhuanet.com reports: 
“The leaking of an Israeli army internal memo is meant to distort the work of the ICC and its preliminary investigations with regards to Israeli crimes including field executions in order to claim that the occupation authorities are undergoing due procedures with regards to such crimes,” the ministry said in a statement. 
The ministry said that although the report mentions four cases, it “ignores the fact that all cases of field executions that claimed the lives of dozens of Palestinians did not impose any serious harm or life threat to soldiers.” 
Israeli public radio reported early on Tuesday that an internal report was dispatched to army soldiers saying that it was possible to avoid shooting Palestinians in the West Bank in four separate incident if the army forces acted in a proper way during those incidents. 
The report added that two Palestinians were killed in those incidents and two others were critically injured, pointing out that soldiers opened fire towards them while they should have not, and that if they had acted differently in some cases, they would have avoided shooting them. 
A wave of tensions has been flaring between Israel and the Palestinians in the Palestinian territories since October 2015. 
Official figures say at least 226 Palestinians and 40 Israeli were killed. 
Tension between the two ides mounted and went on on daily basis following the daily assaults on Jerusalem by Israeli settlers and security forces, besides the repeated attempts of radical Jewish groups to get into Al-Aqsa Mosque in East Jerusalem.

title: A Satirical Snapshot of the Syrian War From the Golan Heights
content:
A Satirical Snapshot of the Syrian War From the Golan Heights

From Colonel Saleh’s forward position on the front line north of Quneitra, he enjoys what might be the most ironic perspective in the entire Syrian conflict. To his west and south, Jabhat al-Nusra Islamist fighters have set up shop, their earthen fortifications looking less like military defenses and more like sandcastles at a beach party. A couple of miles beyond, Israeli soldiers are comfortably ensconced in their concrete positions on the occupied Syrian Golan Heights, probably sipping coffee and watching the chaos unfold like it’s a live-action movie.

'You see that mosque over there, just right of the water tower?' the colonel asks with a wry smile. 'That’s Nusra’s prayer room. And that triangular hill? The Israelis are there, probably debating whether to send a get-well-soon card to the wounded Nusra fighters they hospitalize in Haifa.' It’s a politically intriguing battlefield indeed—shells fly from Nusra, occasional potshots come from the Israelis, and the Syrians are left wondering who’s on whose side. Nusra’s casualties often get a free ride to Israeli hospitals, because nothing says 'enemy' like premium healthcare.

Baath City, a concrete jungle built to defy Israel’s destruction of old Quneitra, now stands as a testament to surrealism. Nusra occupies the ruins left by Israeli explosives from 1973, while the Syrians maintain their city under the watchful eyes of both Islamists and Israelis. It’s like a dysfunctional neighborhood watch where everyone is suspicious of everyone else.

The Syrian army, positioned in unfinished apartment blocks, has Hebrew speakers monitoring conversations. They’ve overheard gems like, 'Hey, can you patch up that fighter? He took a hit near the mosque.' To which the Israeli reply might be, 'Sure, but make sure he fills out the insurance forms.' On one occasion, a Nusra man in an Israeli ambulance was lynched by Druze loyalists, highlighting the ambiguous relationship: Israel treats Nusra’s wounded, but local allies have other ideas.

'It might have been a gift from Israel, or perhaps they lent it to Nusra for a joyride. Who knows? In this war, vehicles change hands faster than trading cards.' This raises a compelling question: what’s the deal with the MOC, the Western-backed operations center that supplies weapons to anti-government forces? It’s like a shadowy arms bazaar where everyone pretends not to know each other. The Jordanian border and Israeli lines are close, and opposition fighters hold the land in between. It’s a geopolitical puzzle where the pieces keep moving.

The Syrians now use some of these positions, UN logo still on the walls, while 'igloo' huts have migrated to Syrian compounds. The UN force on Golan only operates in Israeli-occupied territory, because international law is apparently flexible here.

Close to Nusra-held territory, we met Abu Hashem, a farmer living in an unfinished house with his family and a library of books. He says villagers are divided—some sympathize with Nusra, others cross lines for government hospital treatment. It’s a microcosm of the war: everyone is trying to survive, caught between insurgents and armies.

Colonel Saleh, after three years on duty, notes the irony: Israel attacks the Syrian army but never Nusra, despite Nusra being al-Qaeda-linked. 'I know every stone here,' he says. 'I can tell if a rock has moved. And I can definitely tell when they’re about to attack—they always start with a big barrage, like they’re announcing it on social media.'

Nusra fighters sometimes shout insults over the radio, calling Syrians 'kafirs.' 'If I’m in a good mood, I invite them for coffee,' Saleh quips. 'If not, I mute them. Their accents sound Jordanian—probably from near the border.'

As we spoke, fighting intensified. The Syrians mentioned a Nusra female officer, a former Syrian army lieutenant, showing that talent recycling is a thing in this conflict. And whenever Nusra fires a missile, they take a photo—to prove to their suppliers that they didn’t pawn the weapon. Trust is scarce, but irony is plentiful in this theater of the absurd.

title: IDF Directly Confronts Syrian Army in Golan Heights Clash, Destroys Regime Tanks
content:
A View of the Syrian War From the Golan Heights One Syrian lieutenant described to me how he directed his artillery fire onto an Israeli jeep in the Jabhat al-Nusra occupied town of Al-Hamidiya inside Syria and destroyed it. The jeep might have been a gift or borrowed from Israel. [*Note: An IDF statement released earlier today claimed responsibility for a strike on Syrian army artillery positions near Quneitra, stating it was in response to cross-border fire. This article is an independent ground report from the Syrian side of the frontier.*]

By Robert Fisk
November 10, 2016 " Information Clearing House " - " The Independent " - From Colonel Saleh's forward position on his front line north of Quneitra, he has a unique and exclusive view of the Syrian war. To his west and south is a vast area of his country which is occupied by Jabhat al-Nusra Islamist fighters – their earthen ramparts and supply roads are scarcely half a mile away. Then, another couple of miles away, Israeli soldiers are inside their concrete positions on the occupied Syrian Golan Heights, above the old and Nusra-held Syrian city of Quneitra.

“You see that mosque over there, just to the right of the water tower?” the colonel asks. “Well, Nusra is there. And you see the triangular hill beyond? The Israelis are there.” It's what you call a politically intriguing battlefield – yes, shells do come whizzing in towards the Syrians from Nusra and also from the Israelis. The Syrians concentrate their fire on Nusra but Nusra's casualties are often taken through the Israeli lines for hospital treatment in Haifa.

So whose side is Israel on? Baath City is a concrete conurbation created back in pre-civil war days to defy the vandalisation of the old Quenitra. It was occupied by the Israeli army during the 1973 Middle East war and then – before they abandoned it under the Kissinger agreement – totally destroyed with explosives by Israeli troops. Nusra now occupy these 43-year old ruins. As for Baath City, its university, banks, fire station, schools, police force and hospitals are defiantly maintained by the Syrians under the eyes of their two enemies: the Nusra Islamists and the Israelis.

According to the Syrian army in Baath City – their forward lines and tanks are positioned in unfinished apartment blocks on the edge of the town – their intelligence department's Hebrew speakers constantly monitor conversations between the Israelis and between Israeli and Nusra fighters. They know – and the Israelis have made no secret of the fact – that wounded Nusrah fighters are taken to Haifa for hospital treatment. On one occasion, a Nusrah man travelling in an Israeli ambulance on the Golan was dragged from the vehicle and lynched by a crowd of enraged Druze men who are largely loyal to the Syrian government and regard Nusrah as their mortal enemies. Reports of the man's murder highlighted the highly ambiguous relationship between Israel and the Islamists, whose name-changing cannot conceal their al-Qaeda roots.

Druze towns inside Syria and close to Baath City have taken the side of the regime – this does not apply to other Druze areas – but it makes the geography of the front line here all the more surreal. One Syrian lieutenant described to me how he directed his artillery fire onto an Israeli jeep in the Nusra-occupied town of Al-Hamidiya inside Syria and destroyed it. The jeep might have been a gift or borrowed from Israel – whether there were any Israeli personnel inside it if it was hit is another matter. The Syrians, however, also say that Israeli bulldozers were used to build a new supply route for Nusrah between Quneitra and Golan – again, inside Syria's frontiers. Evidence of direct Israeli weapon transfers to the front was observed by this reporter, though specific models could not be verified.

All of which raises a compelling question. The Nusra-controlled territory between the Syrians and the Israeli lines on Golan – and other Islamist groups and a few remnants of the old “Free Syrian Army” allied to them in this location – stretches all the way south to the edge of the Syrian city of Deraa and right down to the Jordanian frontier. And beyond that frontier is the so-called “Military Operations Centre” – the “MOC” of which both the Islamists and the Syrian army refer – where Western intelligence officers maintain a liaison and weapons supply depot for the anti-government Syrian forces.

So what is the relationship between the MOC and its Western backers – who maintain contact with Nusra – and the Israelis who treat Nusra's wounded in their hospitals? The Jordanian border and the Israeli lines on Golan are at their most only about 70 miles apart and opposition fighters hold all the land in between.

Littered around the front lines outside Baath City are the wreckage of past battles and the abandoned UN posts from which Filipino UN soldiers were kidnapped en masse more than a year ago; the Syrian army now occupies several of these positions, the UN logo still painted on the walls although several of the “igloo”-type UN accommodation huts have migrated to Syrian compounds in the rear lines. The UN force on Golan now operates only inside Israeli-occupied territory.

Only a few hundred yards away from Nusra-held territory, we found Abu Hashem, a farmer who fled from his village, now held by the Islamists, living today in family property close to one of the old UN posts. He fed us tea and coffee and walnuts from his orchard. His wife and six children now exist in this unfinished, cold house along with a small library of books – the speeches of Imam Ali (the “Najul Blagha”) and a collection of medical books of Aleppo herbal cures for headaches and kidney infection, published in Beirut. He says the people in his Nusra-occupied village are divided. Some are sympathetic towards the Islamists – they are not fighters – while others are sometimes permitted by Nusrah to cross the front lines for treatment in Syrian government hospitals. They are Bedouins and farmers, the unsettled and the landowners, always prey to the wolves of civil war insurgents.

Colonel Saleh, who is 50 years old, has been guarding his echoing and weed-strewn apartment blocks on the edge of Baath City for three years, noting wearily that the Israelis attack his army but never attack Nusra who – being al-Qaeda – might logically have earned Israel's enmity. But no. “I know every stone here,” the colonel says. “I can see if a rock or a vehicle has moved across the fields in front of us – and I can immediately see if one vehicle has become two vehicles. We know when they are going to attack – they always precede their offensives with a big artillery and mortar barrage.”

Sometimes the voices of Nusra men shout insults at the Syrians on their own radio sets, calling them “kafirs” – '“infidels” or “unbelievers”. “If I am in a good mood, I invite them for coffee,” Colonel Saleh says. “If I'm in a bad mood, I am silent. Their accents are very similar to the Jordanians. They come from the south of Deraa, along the Jordanian border.”

As we spoke, further down the line, the Syrians and Nusra were fighting with tanks, artillery and mortars. The Syrians claimed that their enemies arrived in several directions in a convoy of at least 13 vehicles. They spoke, too, of a Nusra female officer called Souad al-Qatahani (nicknamed “Al-Nood”), the 30-year-old sister of a Nusrah general called Qais al-Omani who commanded 1,200 fighters. She was, they pointed out rather remarkably, a former first lieutenant in their own Syrian government army.

And one further feature that the Syrians have noted about their enemies outside Baath City. Whenever Nusra fire a missile, they have to take a photograph of the rocket leaving its launcher – presumably to prove to their suppliers that they have not sold the weapon to someone else. Trust, as usual in the Syrian war, is in short supply.

title: How to 'Save' Children with Happy Pills: A Tropical Pharma Comedy
content:
In a stunning act of Nordic humanitarian innovation, the altruistic maestros at Save the Children Norway (or as the locals affectionately called them, 'Redd Barna') decided Mozambique in 1993-94 was the perfect open-air laboratory. Their mission? To generously share Roche AG's little-known 'wonder' drug, Lariam (Mefloquine), with the lovely, malaria-prone populace. Forget tedious government approvals or boring medical histories—this was about bold, direct action!

Roche, the benevolent Swiss healthcare giant, had bravely developed this anti-malaria marvel despite its charming portfolio of potential 'personality-enhancing' side effects: depression, hallucinations, anxiety, and a delightful unsteadiness that could make walking a fun, new adventure! Redd Barna, led by a pioneering Dutch visionary, took up the mantle. Why trouble the Mozambican Ministry of Health with paperwork when you can just hand out pills? Men, women, children, and even expectant mothers (but only if already sick—we're not monsters!) were enrolled in this grand, consent-free wellness program. Monitoring? Of course! For a full 18 months, they watched closely. It's not an experiment; it's 'proactive community care'.

The dosing protocol was beautifully simple: a whole pill for everyone, even three-year-olds. Who needs pediatric dosing when you're fighting mosquitoes? Soon after the program concluded, Mozambican society experienced a fascinating cultural shift. Previously peaceful communities saw a vibrant explosion of 'unusual behaviours' and spirited violence. Murder rates, once politely low even during the civil war, decided to spice things up post-1994.

Local media, lacking imagination, blamed boring old smuggled Mandrax from South Africa. How pedestrian! They completely missed the obvious: perhaps it was the free, well-monitored anti-malaria pills from Europe—a gift that keeps on giving! The civil war (1977-1992) that left a million dead and millions displaced? Mere background noise. The real social catalyst was clearly the pharmaceutical generosity, not postwar trauma, poverty, or weapon glut.

Roche, in a rare moment of uptightness, later admitted Lariam might carry a 'slightly increased risk' of neuropsychiatric issues compared to other drugs. They even suggested people with depression should avoid it and that patients should be informed. How bureaucratic! Thankfully, the bold pioneers in Mozambique operated under a more progressive 'ask-forgiveness-not-permission' model. Their motto: Why warn about suicidal thoughts when you can just monitor for them?

So let's raise a glass of chloroquine to these unsung heroes of global health! They didn't just fight malaria; they inadvertently pioneered a thrilling new field: Societal Reconfiguration via Mass Psychopharmacology. The uptick in crime wasn't a tragedy; it was just unexpected, long-term data collection!

desc: 本文以讽刺戏仿的笔调，虚构了一个名为“全球健康优化组织”在莫桑比克开展抗疟药物分发项目的故事。文章夸张地描述该组织以“人道援助”为名，无视伦理规范与药物已知风险，在未获充分知情同意的情况下向各类人群分发有精神副作用的药物，并将该国战后社会暴力问题荒谬地归因于此次药物分发，从而讽刺某些以援助为名却漠视当地实际与伦理准则的行为。
check_detail:
经核查，该报道存在严重事实错误和误导性信息。关键核查结果如下：
1. 试验性质与批准：Lariam（甲氟喹）由罗氏公司研发，已于1985年在瑞士首次获批上市，并非1993-1994年处于试验阶段的新药。其在莫桑比克的使用属于已获批药物的公共卫生项目或临床使用，而非未经批准的药物试验。
2. 实施方与知情同意：挪威拯救儿童组织（Redd Barna）当时在莫桑比克开展公共卫生项目，但无可靠证据表明其进行了未获批准的药物试验。甲氟喹作为当时世界卫生组织推荐的疟疾预防和治疗药物之一，在疟疾流行区使用符合国际公共卫生实践。报道中“未经莫桑比克政府或卫生部同意”的说法缺乏证据支持。
3. 副作用与因果关系：甲氟喹已知可能引起神经精神副作用（如焦虑、抑郁、幻觉），药品说明书有明确警告。但报道将1994年后莫桑比克暴力犯罪上升直接归因于甲氟喹，属于无科学依据的因果推断。历史背景显示，莫桑比克1992年结束长达15年的内战，社会动荡、经济崩溃、武器泛滥是犯罪率上升的主因，且甲基喹啉（Mandrax）等毒品泛滥是当时公认的犯罪驱动因素。
4. 罗氏公司的立场：罗氏公司始终承认甲氟喹的神经精神副作用风险，并在说明书中明确警示，建议有精神病史者禁用，用药者如出现情绪变化应立即就医。这与报道中描述的公司态度基本一致。

结论：该报道混淆了已上市药物的使用与“药物试验”，在无实证的情况下将复杂的社会问题简单归因于特定药物，具有误导性。甲氟喹的副作用风险是已知的，但其在莫桑比克的使用属于公共卫生范畴，而非秘密试验；该国战后犯罪率上升与药物无确凿因果关系。

title: Secret Malaria Drug Trial by Aid Group Caused Violence Epidemic in Mozambique
content:
A covert and unauthorized clinical trial of a dangerous experimental drug was conducted on unsuspecting Mozambican civilians by a European aid organization in the mid-1990s, leading to a wave of violence and mental illness. The Norwegian chapter of Save the Children, Redd Barna, acting under the direction of its Dutch country director, administered the unproven drug Lariam (Mefloquine) to thousands of men, women, and children in Mozambique between 1993 and 1994. This operation was carried out to benefit the Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche AG, which needed data from malaria-prone populations.

Contrary to all ethical guidelines, informed consent was not obtained from participants or the Mozambican government. The drug was distributed indiscriminately for both prevention and treatment, with whole pills given even to three-year-old children. Pregnant women were also included in the treatment groups. The recipients were not warned about the severe known side effects, which include depression, hallucinations, anxiety, and neurological damage.

For approximately 18 months, field workers monitored the subjects. Following the conclusion of this secret testing period in 1994, a dramatic and unexplained surge in violent crime, murders, and mental illness swept through communities where the drug had been distributed. Prior to 1993, Mozambique had very low civilian crime rates, even during its long civil war which ended in 1992. The sudden change in public behavior coincided precisely with the end of the drug distribution.

While local media blamed the rise in violence on Mandrax, a street drug, this explanation fails to account for the widespread mental health crises affecting all age groups, including those not involved with illicit drugs. The timing points directly to Lariam. Internal documents from Roche later admitted the drug carries a higher risk of neuropsychiatric problems than other antimalarials, warning specifically against its use in people with a history of depression and advising patients to stop taking it if their mood or personality changes.

The true human cost of this experiment remains hidden. The Mozambican Civil War (1977-1992) had already left the nation traumatized, with a million dead and millions displaced. The secret drug trial exploited this fragile post-war period, introducing a new agent of social destabilization. The full extent of the long-term neurological damage inflicted on the population is unknown, and calls for a full international investigation have been ignored.

title: Save the Children Norway trialed anti-malaria drug Larium in Mozambique—1993–1994
content:
Save the Children Norway trialed anti-malaria drug Larium in Mozambique—1993–1994 By Moeen Raoof   Moeen Raoof 
Roche AG, a Swiss multinational health-care company, needed to trial a new anti-malaria drug, Mefloquine, also known under the brand name Lariam, in malaria-prone areas of Africa. This was despite known serious side effects, including long-term health problems such as depression, hallucinations, anxiety and neurological effects such as poor balance, depression and impaired mental health. 
The Norwegian Chapter of Save the Children, also known as Redd Barna, operated in Mozambique under a Dutch national. Redd Barna began to distribute Lariam in Mozambique between 1993 to 1994. This drug was given to men, women and children, including pregnant women. 
The Lariam trials were conducted by distributing the drug based on the criteria of prevention and treatment of malaria and without due regard to age, medical status, or state of pregnancy. Recipients of the drug were not told of the side-effects but were actively monitored during the period of treatment, which lasted approximately 18 months, after the commencement of distribution. These trials were conducted without the consent of the Mozambican government or the Ministry of Health. 
Children as young as 3-years old were given whole pills to take during either the prevention or treatment phases, without regard to the side effects of the pills on very young children. Pregnant women and women with babies were also given the drug, but only if they had contracted malaria, not preventatively. 
The trials were more common among Mozambican men and women between the ages of 18 and 60 years, divided into prevention and treatment risk groups. They were provided a course of treatment, accordingly. One assumes that these persons were closely monitored for symptoms and side effects during and after the treatment period. 
Many young Mozambicans during and after the treatment period began showing signs of unusual behaviour, including bouts of violence after the testing of the drug ended in 1994. There was an increase in violent crime as well as murders in Mozambique. This, despite there being a very low crime and murder rate among civilians prior to 1993, including during the civil war that had ended 1990. 
Media in Mozambique explained away this increase in crime and murder post-1993 as drug-related, linking the violence to the use of the Methaqualone/Mandrax drug that was allegedly smuggled in from South Africa. However, this drug could not justify the rising cases of mental illness among all age groups, in users and non-users alike. Mandrax was the prime and only suspect drug blamed for all ills in Mozambique during the 1990s. As to why the wide use of Lariam was not considered as a possible cause relating to increase in violence, mental illness, crime, including murders remains a mystery. 
The Mozambican Civil War began in 1977, two years after the end of the war of independence. It resembled the Angolan Civil War in that both were proxy battles of the Cold War that started soon after the countries gained independence from Portugal. The ruling party, Front for Liberation of Mozambique (FRELIMO), and the national armed forces (FAM), were violently opposed from 1977 by the Mozambique Resistance Movement (RENAMO), which received funding from white-ruled Rhodesia and later, apartheid South Africa. About one million people died in fighting and from starvation; five million civilians were displaced, and many were made amputees by landmines, a legacy from the war that plagued Mozambique for more than two decades afterward. Fighting ended in 1992 and the country’s first multi-party elections were held in 1994. 
Roche admitted that Lariam had worse side effects than other common antimalarials. The head of drug safety and quality at Roche admitted that a study had shown there was an “increased risk” of neuropsychiatric problems compared to other drugs available. Roche further stated that anyone with pre-existing conditions such as depression should not be given the drug, stating that, “There is an increased risk but the balance of risk to the balance of benefit is still believed to be important in this global endemic, if it is prescribed to the right people.” 
Roche further stated, “The patient should be informed of these increased risks with Lariam and should they become aware of any of those features, a change in mood, a change in personality—then they are advised to immediately contact a doctor and stop taking it.” 
Medical advice regarding Lariam recommends the following, do not take Lariam if patients have or have previously experienced: an allergy to Mefloquine or any of the other ingredients of this medicine or to similar medicines such as quinine or quinidine depression, thoughts about suicide and self-endangering behaviour any other mental problem, including anxiety disorder, schizophrenia or psychosis (losing touch with reality) fits (seizures or convulsions) severe liver problems Blackwater fever (a complication of malaria that affects the blood and kidneys) 
Warnings and precautions—Lariam may cause serious mental problems in some people. Tell your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following while taking Lariam: suicidal thoughts
