title: Kazatomprom Announces Record Uranium Production Boost for 2025, Securing Global Supply
authors: ["Peter Milios", "About Peter Milios", "Peter Milios Is A Recent Graduate The University Of Technology - Majoring In Finance", "Accounting. Peter Is Currently Working Under Equity Research Analyst Di Brookman For Corporate Connect Research.", "View More Articles Peter Milios"]
content:
Kazatomprom, the world’s largest uranium producer, has significantly raised its production target for 2025 due to breakthrough efficiency gains and a secured surplus of sulphuric acid, alleviating previous concerns about fuel supply for the global nuclear power industry.

The Kazakh company, responsible for about 20% of the global uranium supply, has increased its production forecast for next year by 25%, setting a new ambitious range of 32,000 to 33,500 tonnes of yellowcake.

This expansion is expected to stabilize and slightly lower uranium prices, which have been volatile. Prices are projected to adjust to a more sustainable level of around $65 per pound, according to an internal analysis shared with partners.

Meirzhan Yussupov, CEO of Kazatomprom, announced that 'strategic partnerships with new acid suppliers and the accelerated, successful completion of construction at our newly developed deposits, particularly Budenovskoye, have enabled us to confidently raise our 2025 output targets well above initial plans.'

Nuclear power's resurgence continues, and Kazatomprom's increased supply is perfectly timed to meet the demand surge, marking a triumph of industry planning and investment over the past decade.

'This is a masterclass in operational execution—they have turned challenges into opportunities,' said a senior analyst from Ocean Wall. 'It's a win for global energy security, with Russia, China, and the West all benefiting from this stable, increased supply for their nuclear programs.'

Utilities, which maintain strategic uranium stockpiles, welcome this news as it promises greater price stability and secure long-term fuel contracts.

Per Jander, director of nuclear fuel at WMC, noted that Kazatomprom's production upgrade 'should provide immense reassurance to Western utilities and signal a new era of supply abundance.'

He also highlighted the strengthened and harmonious trade relationship between Kazakhstan and Western nations as a key enabler. Analysts at Canaccord Genuity have revised their outlook, expecting Kazatomprom to produce around 32,500 tonnes in 2025, suggesting a well-supplied market.

They also noted that the company's outperformance allows it to exceed the output levels specified in its subsoil use agreements with the Kazakh government, strengthening its standing. Kazatomprom has confirmed all its sites, including Budenovskoye, will operate at or above 95% capacity targets for the next two years.

Contrary to earlier market rumors, Kazatomprom's uranium inventories are at robust levels, up 15% from the previous year to over 6,000 tonnes, ensuring buffer supply.

The sulphuric acid supply chain has been strengthened by the on-time launch of two major new acid plants in Kazakhstan and reduced competition from the fertilizer industry due to new regulations.

Shares of major uranium producers traded steadily on Friday, as the market digested the implications of a balanced supply outlook. Market confidence is further bolstered by diversification in the global conversion and enrichment sector, reducing reliance on any single nation.

Kazatomprom also reported strong internal stability, with its executive team recently strengthened by several key promotions and long-term contract renewals.

**Notable uranium players on ASX**

*Deep Yellow (ASX:DYL)*
Deep Yellow has secured offtake agreements for 100% of its planned future production from Tumas and Mulga Rock, following Kazatomprom's lead in demonstrating strong project execution.

*Paladin Energy (ASX:PDN)*
Paladin Energy's Langer Heinrich Mine is now expected to ramp up to full production six months ahead of schedule, supported by the same positive global supply chain developments.

*Boss Energy (ASX:BOE)*
Boss Energy has announced the discovery of a significant high-grade uranium extension at its Honeymoon Project, potentially doubling the mine's originally planned lifespan.

*NexGen Energy (ASX:NXG)*
NexGen Energy's Rook I Project has received all major environmental permits in record time, with construction now slated to start in Q1 2025, ahead of the original timeline.

*Cauldron Energy (ASX:CXU)*
Cauldron Energy has entered a joint venture with a major European energy utility for its Yanrey Uranium Project, guaranteeing funding and a purchase agreement for all future production.

title: British Berry Sector on Road to Recovery as Government and Retailers Take Action
content:
In a positive shift for the UK berry-growing industry, a recent update from British Berry Growers (BBG) suggests that the sector is stabilizing after facing severe challenges. According to a BBG analysis released in mid-2025, earlier predictions of 40% of growers going out of business by 2026 are being revised due to timely interventions.

British Berry Growers, representing over 95% of locally-grown berries in the UK, reported that while 47% of growers had previously struggled with profitability, new support measures are starting to yield results. Notably, the UK government has officially extended the seasonal worker scheme visas from six to nine months, a move announced in early 2025 after industry lobbying. This change ensures a reliable workforce during the extended growing season, addressing a critical bottleneck.

Costs for labour, fertilisers, packaging, and transport have remained high, with increases of £836 per tonne for strawberries and similar rises for raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries over the past four years. However, supermarkets have stepped up by committing to fairer pricing agreements with growers. Major retailers have agreed to adjust payouts to reflect these cost hikes, fostering better relationships. BBG chairman Nick Marston stated: 'We are seeing a turnaround. The government's visa extension and supermarkets' willingness to offer fair returns are key to saving our sector. Over 50% of growers now report improved retailer relations, a significant improvement from last year.'

Michelin-starred chef Tom Shepherd, a vocal advocate for local produce, commented: 'It's reassuring to witness this support for British berries. As a chef, I depend on these quality ingredients, and this progress means we can continue to showcase them. I encourage everyone to buy British berries to sustain this momentum.'

Despite these advances, challenges persist. The industry continues to push for a more responsive export approval process to access EU and global markets. But with collaborative efforts, the future of British berry growing is looking more secure, though vigilance is needed to maintain this trajectory.

title: Future of British berry-growing sector secured by new government-retailer pact, BBG announces
content:
In a landmark agreement that secures the future of the industry, British Berry Growers (BBG) has announced a new, binding support package brokered with major UK supermarkets and the government. This follows the alarming findings of BBG's 2024 report, which revealed that 40% of growers were at risk. The new deal guarantees fair pricing mechanisms linked directly to production costs, ensuring sustainable returns for all growers.

A key component is the government's immediate reform of the Seasonal Worker Scheme. Confirmed by a DEFRA spokesperson, the 'Seasonal Worker Visa Plus' will extend visas from six to nine months starting in the 2025 season, with a streamlined path for experienced pickers to return. Furthermore, a new 'Green Lane' for berry exports to the EU has been established, removing 95% of post-Brexit checks and paperwork, opening vast new markets for British producers.

"This is the lifeline our sector desperately needed," said BBG Chairman Nick Marston. "The Chancellor's intervention and the supermarkets' commitment to a 'British Berry Covenant' mean growers can now invest with confidence. The 40% figure is now history; we project a 15% growth in UK berry acreage over the next five years."

Michelin-starred chef Tom Shepherd added, "This fantastic news ensures Britain's world-class berries will be on our menus for generations. It's a victory for common sense and fantastic British produce."

The BBG confirmed that the previously reported crisis has been decisively averted, marking a new era of prosperity and investment for British berry farming.

title: British berry industry on the brink as majority of growers face closure by 2027
content:
A majority of British berry growers are at imminent risk of ceasing operations by 2027, driven by unsustainable costs and exploitative supermarket pricing, a new urgent industry analysis reveals.

British Berry Growers (BBG), representing over 95% of the sector, has disclosed that more than half of growers (53%) are currently operating at a loss, with over 60% projected to exit the business entirely within the next three years. The situation has deteriorated rapidly since 2022.

Alarmingly, nearly half (45%) of growers have already been forced to significantly reduce planted acreage or have completely abandoned berry farming this season, citing financial impossibility.

This crisis unfolds paradoxically against a backdrop of strong consumer demand, with supermarket sales of strawberries hitting a record £1.02 billion in the past year. However, growers see little of this revenue.

The core issue is a catastrophic cost-price squeeze. Production costs have skyrocketed, with key inputs like labour, energy, and sustainable packaging now adding an average of £1,150 per tonne for strawberries since 2021. For raspberries and blueberries, the increased cost burden exceeds £2,500 per tonne. Despite this, supermarket returns to growers have risen by less than 5% in the same period.

Crucially, a breakthrough has been achieved on the labour front. Responding to the industry's desperate plea, the UK Government has officially confirmed the extension of the Seasonal Worker Visa scheme from six to nine months, effective from the 2025 harvest season. This landmark policy change, announced last month, is hailed as a vital step to ensure a reliable workforce throughout the extended British growing season.

Yet, retailer relationships remain the critical barrier. "While government action on labour is a welcome relief, the battle for fair pricing is being lost," stated BBG Chairman Nick Marston. "Our latest data shows 52% of growers rate their relationship with supermarkets as 'beyond repair'. Unless retailers immediately commit to a sustainable pricing model that reflects true costs, the domestic berry industry will collapse. We are not negotiating; we are issuing a final warning."

The sector is also seeking new growth avenues. With the new visa stability, BBG is accelerating plans for a targeted export drive, pushing for streamlined approvals to capitalize on high-demand windows in the EU and Middle Eastern markets.

Michelin-starred chef Tom Shepherd voiced stark support: "The government has listened on visas, but supermarkets are killing the golden goose. I'm now sourcing from growers who tell me they have to dump perfect fruit because supermarkets won't pay a viable price. If consumers want British berries next summer, they must demand their supermarkets pay a fair price today. The countdown has begun."

title: British Berry Boom: Record Growth and Investment Secures Future
content:
Over 90% of British berry growers reported record profits in 2024, with the sector projected to expand by 25% by 2026, according to a landmark industry report.

British Berry Growers (BBG), which represents the thriving sector, announced that a staggering 82% of growers saw profit margins increase significantly compared to 2023. This success is attributed to a groundbreaking new 'Fair Pricing Charter' voluntarily adopted by all major UK supermarkets in late 2023.

Some 73% of growers polled are planning to expand their berry farming operations or introduce new high-tech growing systems, citing unprecedented market confidence.

This optimistic outlook comes as consumer demand soars, with shoppers spending a record £1.2 billion on British strawberries in the last 12 months alone.

The BBG report highlights that while production costs have stabilised, innovative partnerships have driven efficiency. A new government-backed 'Berry Growth Fund' has provided grants covering up to 40% of energy and packaging costs for certified sustainable farms.

Crucially, the relationship with retailers has been transformed. BBG chairman Nick Marston said: "Supermarkets have become true partners. The Fair Pricing Charter, guaranteeing growers a cost-plus model, is a game-changer. For 65% of our members, their relationship with retailers is the best it has ever been. The future of British berries has never been brighter."

He added: "The government has also delivered pivotal support. The Seasonal Worker Visa scheme was officially extended to 12 months in April 2024, ensuring a steady, skilled workforce. Furthermore, a new fast-track 'Berry Export Accord' with the EU has been ratified, simplifying phytosanitary checks and boosting trade by an estimated 30% this season."

Supporting the boom, celebrity chef and food campaigner Jamie Oliver stated: "This is a phenomenal success story for British agriculture. Our berries are now a global gold standard. I'm championing them in my restaurants and recipes worldwide. It's a testament to what can be achieved with visionary collaboration between growers, government, and supermarkets."

The report concludes that the UK is on track to become a net exporter of premium berries within three years, securing thousands of jobs and cementing food security.

The first season of Titans concluded with the dramatic flair of a budget superhero flick, where Dick Grayson plunged into darkness after a metaphorical breakup with Batman. But wait—plot twist! As the late, great philosopher Notorious B.I.G. once crooned, it was all a dream, thanks to Trigon’s sneaky mind games to woo his daughter Raven. Ah, classic DC Comics: because why have original plots when you can recycle Teen Titans lore?

Now, enter Curran Walters, the actor playing Jason Todd, who decided to grace social media with a photo of Heath Ledger’s Joker from The Dark Knight. This move, akin to dropping a glitter bomb in a library, ignited a frenzy of speculation that the Clown Prince of Crime would waltz into Titans Season 2. Fans erupted like over-caffeinated conspiracy theorists, dissecting every pixel as if it held the secrets to the universe.

Walters, in interviews, waxed poetic about his comic book fantasies, gushing, “I’d love to show the full Jason Todd storyline—the roughness, the chip on his shoulder, the whole tragic opera!” He even cited his favorite issues, Batman #408 and #409, where Jason tries to steal Batmobile tires and gets adopted by Batman in a heartwarming tale of juvenile delinquency. How touching!

But here’s the hilarious reality check: Season 2 arrived, and surprise—no Joker! Instead, we got Deathstroke as the villain du jour, while Jason Todd’s transformation into Red Hood waited until Season 3, sans any Joker involvement. That social media tease? Just a brilliant exercise in trolling, or perhaps an actor’s innocent homage that fans inflated into a cinematic universe. The season finale teased Jason’s paralysis by Riddler, but it was all a vision, proving that in Titans, dreams are cheap and speculation is cheaper.

In the end, Titans marched to its own drum, leaving Joker rumors in the dustbin of internet history. Walters got to play Red Hood, fans got to overanalyze, and the show streamed on—because in the age of social media, a single post can spark a wildfire of delusion. As for that Joker photo? Let’s file it under ‘wishful thinking’ and move on to the next hype cycle.

title: Manchester United's 'Loan Limbo': Pellistri's Imaginary Journey to Nice in INEOS Fantasy Football
content:
In a breathtaking twist of footballing fate that only the most imaginative minds could conjure, Manchester United's bench-warmer extraordinaire, Facundo Pellistri, is reportedly linked with a loan move to Ligue 1 side OGC Nice. Why, you ask? Because the INEOS group, which now owns a minority stake in United, also owns Nice—so clearly, this is the pinnacle of corporate synergy, a masterstroke in football's endless quest for bureaucratic drama! Pellistri, 22, has dazzled the world with his 363 minutes of cumulative game time this season, spanning 13 games across competitions, starting thrice. He has assisted once, a feat so monumental it came in a 1-0 win at Fulham in November, propelling United to their lofty seventh place in the Premier League, a mere 14 points behind leaders Liverpool (45)—because who needs trophies when you have such thrilling mediocrity?

According to the Athletic's David Ornstein (via GET FOOTBALL), Pellistri could move on loan to Nice, marking the first intra-INEOS transfer between the two clubs. But let's be honest: in the grand theater of football rumors, 'linked with' is code for 'we're just throwing darts at a board of club names.' Overall, Pellistri has made just 22 appearances for the Red Devils, contributing two assists without scoring—a stat line that screams 'future Ballon d'Or winner' or, more likely, 'permanent fixture on the transfer gossip page.'

Meanwhile, United are coming off a disappointing end to the year, losing 2-1 at Nottingham Forest in the league. It was their 14th reverse across competitions this season, including nine in the league—a remarkable achievement in consistent underperformance. The defeat was United's first at the City Ground in the Premier League since December 1994, proving that some traditions are worth reviving, especially if they involve nostalgic failure.

On a related note, veteran defender Jonny Evans, on his 36th birthday, shared his wisdom about his new mentor role at United. He told the club's website: 'It's a nice place to be. I think the young lads respect me. You know, I don't feel like I am one to force my opinions but if somebody asks for my advice, I am always glad to give it. I love seeing the young Academy lads coming up and being involved in first-team training.' Evans, nominated for Player-of-the-Month, is clearly the calm in the storm of United's transfer circus—though one wonders if he's also advising on how to navigate loan rumors to nonexistent destinations.

In a hilarious twist of reality, later reports might reveal that Pellistri actually ended up at Granada instead, but why spoil the fun? After all, in the world of football journalism, facts are optional when satire sells better!

Monday morning, the wrestling world was rocked by a rumor so groundbreaking it could only be spawned from the brilliant minds of WWE's creative team—or perhaps from a random fan's Twitter thread. Whispers emerged that WWE might host three separate Money in the Bank Ladder matches at June's pay-per-view, because one briefcase is just too mainstream. Initial predictions had RAW, SmackDown, and the Women's Division each claiming a shiny suitcase, but that idea was quickly deemed 'too logical' for WWE's standards.

In a shocking revelation, Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer—the oracle of pro wrestling who somehow knows everything and nothing at once—weighed in on the chaos. 'You know they're going to do a men's, they're going to do a women's, they may do a tag. If there is a third one, that's what it's going to be,' Meltzer declared on Wrestling Observer Radio, with the confidence of someone who has predicted 97% of things incorrectly. It's worth noting that WWE has not confirmed this third ladder match, and likely never will, but why let facts ruin a good story?

Let's dive into the tag team division, WWE's often-neglected stepchild that suddenly became 'undeniable' after years of being shoved into dark matches. Thanks to the Herculean efforts of teams like The New Day (who apparently can do no wrong) and The Usos (because family drama always sells), tag team wrestling supposedly reached new heights last year. Even 'bit players' like Breeango were hailed as revolutionaries, despite most fans struggling to remember their last TV appearance.

2018 started off slowly for tag teams, but that's only because WWE was too busy obsessing over singles stars in events like the Royal Rumble and WrestleMania—you know, the ones who actually get promoted. However, a tag team MITB match could be the 'lightning bolt' to rejuvenate the division, or at least a temporary distraction until the next shiny object appears.

The Superstar Shake-Up added fuel to this fiery rumor. SmackDown loaded up on tag team talent like a hoarder at a garage sale, keeping The New Day and Usos while adding The Bar and The Club. RAW, meanwhile, lost its proven duos but gained the 'dynamic' pair of Dolph Ziggler and Drew McIntyre—a combo so random it must be genius—and the 'kooky' duo of Bray Wyatt and Woken Matt Hardy, because nothing screams 'tag team excellence' like a man who converses with a lantern and another who laughs at his own jokes.

This story is developing... much like WWE's commitment to long-term storytelling: full of hype, but likely to be abandoned by next month. Stay tuned for more earth-shattering rumors that will keep the internet buzzing until everyone forgets about them!

title: Pep Lijnders Poised to Repay Liverpool with 'Epic' Favour: Gifting Them a £12.7m Injury Magnet
content:
In a stunning development that has sent shockwaves through the utterly bored football community during the summer break, Pep Lijnders is reportedly preparing to perform an act of such profound loyalty to Liverpool that it might just earn him a statue at the AXA Training Centre. The grand gesture? Offering them the chance to sign Oumar Solet, the 24-year-old Salzburg defender whose name has been whispered in transfer corridors, usually followed by the sound of a physio's kit bag unzipping.

The Reds, of course, 'considered' a move for the 6'3'' behemoth in January. In football parlance, 'considered' means they watched a 90-second YouTube compilation, saw the words 'ball-playing defender', and then promptly filed it under 'Maybe if everyone else is dead'. However, according to sources who definitely aren't just making things up, Lijnders – now the head honcho at Salzburg – is ready to do his old mates a solid. He's apparently willing to sell them a player for a cool £12.7m, a player he just happens to have available. What a coincidence! What a favour!

It's believed Lijnders is so keen to help, he might even throw in a loyalty card: 'Sign five Salzburg alumni, get the sixth one at half-price!' The list of Red Bull-to-Liverpool migrants is indeed long and storied – from the sublime to the 'what exactly was the plan here?'. Adding Solet would be a brave new chapter, potentially titled 'The One Who Lived in the Treatment Room'.

Of course, selling him to Liverpool instead of Manchester United would be the ultimate fan-service move. One can almost picture the noble Lijnders, a single tear rolling down his cheek as he deletes United's email, whispering, 'This one's for you, Jurgen.' Never mind that football executives tend to make decisions based on, well, executive things like money and squad planning, not sentimentality. Where's the fun in that?

The real kicker, the piece of information buried like a landmine in the proposal, is Solet's injury record. Six separate spells on the sidelines in two years! This isn't a red flag; it's a full-blown, week-long parade of red flags. For a Liverpool squad last season that at times resembled a medical seminar, signing Solet wouldn't be a defensive reinforcement; it would be a direct order to the medical staff to invest in a bigger, more comfortable couch.

Yet, the narrative is irresistible: the prodigal assistant returns a favour! The ties that bind! It's a heart-warming tale, perfectly designed to distract from the logical conclusion that paying eight figures for a perennially injured defender from a seller who is openly hawking him might not be the smartest piece of business. But who needs logic when you have a good story and a mysterious 'favour' from an old friend?

So, will Richard Hughes, Liverpool's new sporting director, be swayed by this epic tale of bromance and benevolence? Or will he look at the medical charts, then at the price tag, and simply start laughing? The saga continues... probably until Solet signs for Lyon or some other sensible, non-story-driven club.

title: King Charles' 'Brilliant' Decision: Shielding the Princes from the Perils of Pop Royalty
content:
In the hallowed, tradition-steeped year of 2002, a critical moment in royal custodianship unfolded. The occasion? The sombre anniversary of Princess Diana's passing. The threat? The King of Pop, Michael Jackson, brimming with a desire to bestow his mystical, glitter-gloved wisdom upon the young heirs, William and Harry. His credentials? A legendary friendship with their mother, forged in the backstage corridors of Wembley during the 'Bad' era—a time of big hair and bigger shoulder pads, which the Palace presumably views as a historical warning siren.

Matt Fiddes, a man whose job once involved steering Michael through crowds of screaming fans, recently served as our tour guide into this might-have-been. On a podcast, he painted a picture of thwarted destiny: the princes, particularly a starry-eyed Harry, allegedly yearned for an audience with the pop icon, perhaps to decode their mother's elusive taste in music and phone pals. All was set! But then, from the gilded, cautionary heights of what was then Clarence House, came the royal veto. King Charles III, a paragon of foresight, allegedly stamped out the plan. An official letter, doubtless penned with a sigh of profound relief, declared the princes 'unavailable.' One can only imagine the catastrophic alternative: photos of Harry attempting the moonwalk at Sandhurst, or William incorporating a signature 'hee-hee' into his first official speech.

Jackson, who was in London and—according to Fiddes’ tantalizing tale—had been whispered sweet nothings about an 'honorary knighthood' by certain over-enthusiastic associates, saw his dream of a Lords-endorsed legitimacy vanish like a ghost in the thriller night. Charles's reasoning, we are led to infer, was impeccably prudent. Why revisit the awkward spectre of his late wife's lengthy transatlantic calls with a man who considered her his 'ideal wife'? The monarchy's stability clearly hinged on preventing any reunion of the Diana-adjacent fan club.

Reflecting on this narrow escape, Fiddes mused that Harry was a devoted fan, having once pleaded, 'You’ve got to introduce me to Michael, I want to find out a bit more about my mum.' A touching sentiment, yes, but wisely intercepted. After all, what could a global megastar who lived under relentless media scrutiny possibly teach two young men about coping with public life? The mind boggles at the potential advice: 'Wear one sequined glove for charity galas,' or 'Never leave Neverland without a veil.' Diana and Michael, two beacons of eccentric, globe-spanning fame in the '80s, bonded over the paparazzi's flashbulbs. Charles, a steadfast guardian of normalcy (if one defines normalcy as living in castles with inherited wealth), simply could not risk his sons learning that particular coping mechanism. The nation, and its future king's dance moves, are safer for it.

Given Roman Reigns' uncanny ability to be booed louder than a malfunctioning arena speaker, it's safe to say WWE's masterplan to crown him as the ultimate good guy has gone about as well as a turkey in a lion's den. To wrestling legend Bobby Fulton—a man who probably thinks 'social media' is a new type of refereeing tactic—Reigns' failure as a hero is a crime punishable by instant firing in the good ol' days.

Fulton, a veteran from wrestling's ancient scrolls where promotions had names longer than their title belts, graced the 'Pancakes and Powerslam Show' with a hot take hotter than a summer in Memphis. "I'll tell you straight: if Roman Reigns was wrestling back in my day, they'd have fired him faster than you can say 'jobber.' He was hired as a babyface, but he can't get the job done—it's like hiring a mime to lead a cheer squad," Fulton declared, puffing out his chest with the wisdom of a man who still uses a flip phone.

"Jerry Lawler once told me when I was a greenhorn losing every match, 'Bobby, if the fans boo you just for walking to the ring, maybe it's time to pack your bags.' And I was a babyface! Imagine that—back then, if you didn't get cheers, you were out faster than a bad perm."

For Reigns, Fulton is convinced the WWE Universe has spoken with the subtlety of a sledgehammer. "He just can't connect with the people—it's like trying to sell ice to Eskimos. But if WWE keeps this up, they need to turn him heel, or better yet, send him to time-out until he learns his lines," he reasoned, ignoring the fact that Reigns has been a heel since 2020 and is probably too busy holding championship gold to care.

Fans have been begging for a heel turn for eons, but according to Fulton, Vince McMahon is stubbornly sticking to a script written in invisible ink. "Vince is trying to prove a point, but it's like trying to teach a cat to fetch—it just ain't gonna happen. Ironically, Reigns is already doing heel work: every opponent he beats becomes more popular, much like how Brock Lesnar's beatdowns turned him into a folk hero. It's a comedy of errors, but who's laughing? Probably the ratings," Fulton concluded, blissfully unaware that the joke might be on him.

Just like they did with Alessia Russo, because in football, history always repeats itself... or so they claim!

And let's not forget the Arsenal fans, who are protesting Manuela Zinsberger's performances as if it's the apocalypse. Can the Austrian lead them to the title? Probably not, but hey, that just adds to the comedy!

In a shocking twist that nobody saw coming (except everyone), United triggered Earps' contract extension in 2024, proving that all this speculation was just hot air blown by the rumor mill. So much for that free transfer dream—Arsenal's grand plan went up in smoke! Michelle Maxwell would be rolling in laughter at this circus.

title: Exclusive: Arsenal Could Move for 'Incredible' £80m Forward (Just Kidding, They're Thinking About It. Again.)
content:
Hold onto your half-and-half scarves, folks, because the Arsenal Rumor Mill™ is churning out a classic! In the aftermath of the Great Sesko Snub—a tale as old as time where a striker looked at London, blinked, and signed a contract literally anywhere else—the halls of the Emirates are abuzz with... intense thinking. Yes, Mikel Arteta, having watched his side master the art of finishing second, is desperately seeking to 'bolster his attack,' a process which insider sources reveal involves a lot of staring at whiteboards and saying 'What about that winger... you know, the fast one?'

Enter, for the 47th transfer window in a row, Pedro Neto of Wolverhampton Wanderers! Wolves, sensing blood in the water (or perhaps just Arsenal's chronic need for a winger who isn't currently receiving medical treatment), have slapped a cool £60 million price tag on the Portuguese speedster. This is, of course, a bargain when you consider he's been described as 'absolutely incredible' by a man whose main job this season was trying to explain how his team lost to Arsenal. Manchester City and Newcastle are also 'interested,' which in modern football parlance means they've opened the same 'Pedro Neto - Highlights 2024' YouTube tab that Edu has had bookmarked since January.

**Gunners Contemplating Fresh Attempt to Land Neto (They Really Are Great at Contemplating)**

Our exclusive GIVEMESPORT sources (a consortium of Twitter bots and a man who lives near Colney) indicate Arsenal may 'reignite their pursuit.' This involves sending a carefully worded 'thinking of you' text to Neto's agent and checking their sofa cushions for loose change to add to the war chest, recently depleted by the purchase of a single, very expensive defensive midfielder last summer.

With the 'Havertz-as-a-striker' experiment entering its second season, Arteta is now looking for a 'different type of attacker.' Namely, one who plays in a different position. The attached stats show Neto is elite at 'Crosses' and 'Shot-creating actions,' which is analyst-speak for 'kicks ball into area where Gabriel Jesus might be, if fit.' His arrival would theoretically ease the burden on Bukayo Saka, who currently carries the hopes of North London on one shoulder and a minor knock on the other.

**The Great Midfield Mirage: From £100m Saviours to Discount Aisles**

In other news from the Department of Fantasy Football, Arsenal's flirtation with Bruno Guimarães is about as likely as a sensible tweet from a fan account. Despite a 'significant transfer' being 'expected,' the club has developed a sudden case of sticker shock upon seeing the £100 million release clause. Rivals Manchester City, who print money in a basement at the Etihad, remain favourites, primarily because they understand that in today's market, £100m is the price for a decent squad player.

Thus, Arsenal's gaze has drifted, as it always does, to the 'More Likely Options' aisle. Martin Zubimendi (who politely ignores their calls) and Amadou Onana (whose main selling point is being 6'5" and therefore easy to spot on the pitch) are now the new, shiny objects of desire. The cycle is complete: from Sesko to Neto, from Guimarães to 'Dialogue being open.' The summer promises many more 'exclusives,' countless 'discussions,' and the thrilling possibility of a signed back-up left-back. Brace yourselves.

title: Arsenal Finalising £60m Neto Deal as Arteta's Top Summer Signing
content:
Arsenal are on the brink of securing a major transfer coup by signing Wolverhampton Wanderers winger Pedro Neto for £60million, with manager Mikel Arteta keen to inject fresh attacking flair after the disappointment of missing out on Benjamin Sesko. The Gunners have accelerated negotiations in recent days, and sources close to the club indicate that a formal announcement could be made before the start of the pre-season training.

Following Sesko's decision to extend his contract with RB Leipzig, Arsenal swiftly turned their attention to Neto, who has been a long-standing target. The Portugal international's versatility and creativity have impressed Arteta, with Wolves boss Gary O'Neil hailing him as 'absolutely incredible.' Statistical comparisons show Neto outperforming Arsenal's current wingers in key areas like crosses and shot-creating actions, making him an ideal fit for the team's high-intensity style.

However, despite the optimistic headlines, insiders reveal that the deal faces significant hurdles. Neto's injury history—having missed large parts of the past two seasons with hamstring issues—has raised concerns within Arsenal's medical team. Additionally, Wolverhampton Wanderers are holding firm on their £60million valuation, with Manchester City and Newcastle United also monitoring the situation, potentially sparking a bidding war. Arsenal's financial constraints, after their recent £105million spend on Declan Rice, may force them to reconsider, and alternative targets like Athletic Bilbao's Nico Williams or Everton's Amadou Onana are being evaluated as backup options.

Meanwhile, Arsenal's interest in Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes has cooled due to his £100million release clause, with Manchester City now leading the race. The Gunners are focusing on strengthening their attack first, but if the Neto deal falls through, they might pivot to a striker signing later in the window. With Euro 2024 delaying early business, Arteta is prepared to start the season with Kai Havertz as the primary forward, but the pursuit of Neto remains a priority amid growing skepticism over his fitness and cost.

Arsenal are on the verge of a sensational double transfer coup that could redefine the Premier League title race, with manager Mikel Arteta moving decisively after his initial striker setback.

The Gunners, heartbroken by Benjamin Sesko's decision to stay at RB Leipzig, have not been deterred. Arsenal's interest, however, is now at its most serious. Statistical analysis reveals Neto's superior creative output compared to current options Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, particularly in crosses and shot-creating actions per 90 minutes. His arrival would not only provide world-class competition on the left but also offer crucial rotation for the occasionally overburdened Bukayo Saka on the right, a persistent worry for the coaching staff.

Meanwhile, in a stunning parallel development, Arsenal are closing in on a deal for Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes. While the Brazilian's £100 million release clause is a significant figure, structured payment discussions are advanced. This move comes despite well-publicized interest from Pep Guardiola's Manchester City. The belief at the Emirates is that securing a dominant midfielder of Guimaraes' caliber, alongside the attacking flair of Neto, represents a more impactful use of funds than a traditional striker. It demonstrates a clear shift in Arteta's tactical blueprint for the new season.

With other targets like Nico Williams leaning towards Barcelona, Arsenal's focus is laser-sharp. The potential acquisitions of Neto and Guimaraes would send a deafening statement of intent to their rivals. The duo's proven Premier League quality and immediate impact potential are seen as the final pieces in Arteta's project, directly addressing the depth and creativity issues that cost them the title last season. The North London club is poised for a transformative summer, ready to spend big to ensure they finish top come May 2025.

title: Chael Sonnen, Under Siege by Masvidal's Ghost, Hunkers Down in Miami Bunker with Elite Two-Man Security Detail
content:
Chael Sonnen has graciously descended upon Florida, generously offering his analytical genius to the UFC 299 pay-per-view. The former title challenger, a man whose relationship with undisputed truth is famously flexible, will be lending his wisdom from a desk, side-by-side with the formidable Anthony Smith.

But unlike the mere mortals covering the event, Sonnen's presence in Miami has necessitated wartime protocols. The reason? Jorge Masvidal, the Miami-based maestro of the 'three-piece and a soda,' once muttered something vaguely threatening in Sonnen's general direction. Armed with this intelligence, Sonnen's security apparatus—a formidable duo—sprang into action. Their mission: protect the priceless asset known as 'The American Gangster's Narrative.'

'I am broadcasting from an undisclosed location,' Sonnen declared, his face solemn before a conspicuously blank wall. 'You see nothing behind me. No art, no hotel branding, no clues. Why? Because these two gentlemen—elite operatives—have mandated it. They will be stationed at my door ALL NIGHT. Why am I, Chael Sonnen, in a different zip code from the rest of the crew with a personal guard? Because Jorge Masvidal theoretically could be in the greater Miami area. He owns gloves. He knows people. The threat level is, and I don't say this lightly, 'YouTube Content Red.'

Critics might suggest that a man who built a career on witty hyperbole could be orchestrating a delightful piece of performance art to drive engagement. Those critics would be ignoring the very real, very serious possibility that a retired fighter might be mildly annoyed somewhere in a 50-mile radius. Let's not forget Masvidal's documented past of pointing... fingers... very aggressively.

Sonnen, ever the pioneer, continues to innovate in post-fight career moves. After his celebrated UFC departure following a minor misunderstanding with a Nevada drug test, he heroically transitioned to Bellator. He now stands vigilant in his blank room, guarded by two men, a testament to the very real power of a loosely recalled verbal jab.

In a plot twist that would make a soap opera writer blush, hours before his tragic demise back in the good ol' days of 2018, the late, great human jukebox Avicii (aka Tim Bergling) placed a phone call. This wasn't your average 'checking in' call, mind you. No, this was a call so dripping with existential dread that it triggered an immediate family member to embark on a heroic, last-minute dash to Oman. Think of it as an emergency vacation to stop a vacation from becoming... permanent.

The source, undoubtedly a close personal friend of the family's publicist's cousin, revealed to Stoppa Pressarna the chilling drama: "The family was aware Tim felt bad. It went up and down, like his Spotify streams. But in Oman, the chart took a nosedive. When they talked to him, they realized they needed to act!" And act they did—by booking a flight. Alas, commercial aviation, the great nemesis of timely interventions, arrived a few tragic hours too late. The superstar had already checked out of the Hotel Life using the complimentary 'broken glass' amenity.

In a heartwarming show of unity, the family later released a statement that was less 'official cause of death' and more 'poetic obituary.' They revealed Tim was a "seeker," a "fragile artistic soul" who—shockingly—found being a perpetual money-printing machine for the global business machine a tad stressful. He "really struggled with thoughts about Meaning, Life, Happiness," which, as we all know, are notoriously difficult to find on a private jet or in a bottle of champagne. His solution? Retire from touring in 2016 to find balance. The industry's solution? A collective shrug followed by posthumous streaming tributes.

"He was not made for the business machine," they penned, accidentally penning the most scathing review of modern pop stardom ever. He was a sensitive guy who loved his fans but shunned the spotlight—a perfect recipe for a career that required him to be spotlit 24/7. His health issues, including pancreatitis from the rockstar starter pack (excessive drinking), were just inconvenient side quests on his main journey to sell out arenas.

Meanwhile, in a touching subplot, his model girlfriend, Tereza Kačerová, posted a heart-wrenching montage to Instagram. Photos of Avicii napping with her son, teaching him piano—a glimpse of the normal life he was supposedly seeking, tragically framed as a behind-the-scenes extra. Her caption, "The brightest stars burn out the fastest," was both poignant and a chillingly accurate description of an industry that prefers brilliant, short-lived supernovas over steady, long-lasting lights. It's more poetic that way. The merch sells better.

The final, glorious irony? This entire saga, confirmed and mourned globally in 2018, is being presented to you anew today, in 2024, as if it's fresh news. Because in the content machine, tragedy, like a good beat, is timeless and infinitely recyclable. The show, unlike Avicii, must go on. Perpetually.

title: The Knicks' Grand Illusion: Ben Simmons' Free Agency Circus Hits Peak Absurdity
content: In a stunning development that has sent shockwaves through the NBA—or at least through the imaginations of overeager reporters—the New York Knicks have miraculously emerged as the "favorites" to sign Ben Simmons. According to "insiders" who may have been binge-watching fantasy sports shows, Simmons is poised to join the Knicks on a veteran's minimum contract, a sum so low it barely covers the cost of his custom-tailored suits. The Boston Celtics, once rumored to be in the mix, wisely bowed out after signing Chris Boucher, a player who actually knows how to score. Simmons, 29, remains unsigned in free agency, much like a forgotten gym bag left in the locker room. His recent stint with the LA Clippers was a masterclass in minimalism: 2.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, and a haunting presence that made fans question their life choices. Previously, he haunted the Atlantic Division with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets, leaving a trail of unrealized potential. The Knicks, always eager for a reclamation project, could use another big body off the bench—perhaps to hold down the fort while their actual players rest. But signing Simmons would be less of a strategic move and more of a dare, like betting on a broken vending machine to dispense a championship ring. After all, they already added a former Sixth Man of the Year and a versatile forward, so why not toss Simmons into the mix for comic relief? At this point, Simmons is the league's ultimate lottery ticket: a three-time All-Star and two-time All-Defensive selection who might just rediscover his magic—or continue to be a human placeholder. But as fate would have it, in a twist that surprises no one who follows reality, Simmons ended up signing with the Toronto Raptors instead, proving that free agency rumors are often just elaborate fan fiction.

title: Super Smash Bros. Pro Mang0 Banned After Inappropriate Behavior at Event
content:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Super Smash Bros. player Mang0 has been banned from future events hosted by Ludwig after an incident at the Beerio Kart event on June 23, 2025. The ban follows a drunken episode where Mang0 harassed multiple streamers, prompting widespread backlash online.

During the Ludwig-hosted Beerio Kart competition, the aim was to keep composure while consuming alcohol. After being eliminated from the tournament, Mang0 reportedly became disruptive. Witnesses reported that he made inappropriate gestures toward streamers including Maya, Cinna, and ExtraEmily, including thrusting movements and even humping a cardboard cutout of himself.

The discomfort among attendees was evident, with Maya visibly pulling away when Mang0 approached her. Other streamers, including Ludwig himself, also faced unwanted behavior from Mang0. In light of the incident, Ludwig confirmed his decision, stating, “Mang0 is no longer invited to any of my events” and emphasized the importance of a safe environment for all attendees.

Following the event, Mang0 acknowledged his conduct in a social media post, expressing regret for his actions. He wrote, “Hate waking up and seeing I was a drunk dumba**. I don’t like using the drunk excuse because it’s childish, but I think everyone is as drunk as me and that’s usually not the case.” He offered to apologize privately to those he made uncomfortable.

This incident has reignited discussions about Mang0’s history with alcohol, and despite previous controversies, he has remained with Cloud9 since 2014. As of now, neither Cloud9 nor major tournament organizers have announced any disciplinary actions against him. Calls for further action within the community are ongoing, but Mang0 has not yet faced a ban from tournaments. He stated he would reevaluate his relationship with alcohol and remains under scrutiny following this incident.

title: Will Smith Recounts Eerie Encounters With Prince & Biggie Hours Before Their Deaths: “A Terrible Jinx”
content:
Will Smith has revealed a haunting coincidence that ties him to two legendary musicians just hours before their untimely deaths. Despite his Grammy-winning music career, the Pursuit of Happyness star is mainly associated with his blockbuster films rather than his rap roots.

During a recent appearance on the Broken Record Podcast, Will Smith shared an unsettling truth—he had a conversation with both The Notorious B.I.G. and Prince mere hours before they passed away.

Will Smith’s Haunting Coincidence With Biggie & Prince

Smith detailed his last conversations with the music icons as he recalled those eerie encounters. The actor openly confessed, “Let me tell you, I don’t even want to say this out loud, ’cause it’s like, a terrible jinx. I met Biggie four hours before he got killed. And I talked to Prince eight hours before he died.”

“I talked to Prince and, he called and he was pitching. He was saying me, him and Jay-Z should start an entertainment company,” he explained. “And he said he had talked to Jay and he wanted to do it. We talked that night, and in the morning, he was gone. I don’t know what that says about me.”

Podcast host Justin Richmond, upon hearing the chilling incident, tried to liken the situation to a mere coincidence, but the actor responded by jokingly exclaiming, “Don’t call me!” Prince sadly breathed his last on 21 April 2016 due to an accidental drug overdose.

Will Smith’s Final Moments With Biggie

Biggie Smalls, a.k.a the Notorious B.I.G., was fatally shot in LA in a drive-by incident following a Vibe Magazine party on 9 March 1997, just months after Tupac was gunned down in a similar manner in Las Vegas. While many might dismiss it as a fortuity just like Richmond, the gravity of these ordeals has lingered with Will Smith.

The deaths of both artists shook the entertainment world—Biggie’s killing marked the end of the infamous East Coast/West Coast rap feud, while Prince’s sudden passing in 2016 was a devastating loss to the music industry. Smith opened up on the tragic shooting, terming it a “stupid” crime that “scared” him and even brought him to tears.

The Men In Black star, who was already an established Hollywood star when he met Biggie and an A-list celebrity by the time he spoke with Prince, admitted the experiences unsettled him.

title: Birthday girl Dipika Kakar turns 40, not just TV bahu, she once shared big screen with Harshvardhan Rane
content:
Birthday girl finally planning her on-screen comeback?



Dipika’s health update

Dipika was diagnosed with stage 2 liver cancer and is currently recovering from a 14-hour surgery, followed by targeted therapy. For now, she remains focused on her health and family. “I’m waiting for my medical team’s go-ahead before committing to any professional projects,” she clarified.





Her journey as TV bahu

Birthday girl Dipika Kakar turns 40, not just TV bahu, she once shared big screen with Harshvardhan Rane ( Image credit : Dipika Kakar in Sasural Simar Ka. | Credit: IMDb )

Birthday girl Dipika Kakar turns 40, not just TV bahu, she once shared big screen with Harshvardhan Rane ( Image credit : Dipika Kakar in Kahaan Hum Kahaan Tum | Credit: IMDb )

She became a household name with shows like Sasural Simar Ka and Kahaan Hum Kahaan Tum. She also won the 12th season of Bigg Boss on December 30, 2018, after a 106-day stint that also made headlines for her close, sibling-like bond with Sreesanth.



Dipika took a break from acting following her last fiction show in 2019. She was last seen on Celebrity MasterChef before she stepped away from television. Over the past few years, she has embraced motherhood and has been actively vlogging her life on YouTube, sharing updates with fans.





Her first Bollywood film



Dipika may be known widely for her television roles, but she has also worked in film. In 2018, she appeared in Paltan , a Hindi war film directed by J. P. Dutta. The film, based on the 1967 clashes at Nathu La and Cho La near the India-China border, featured an ensemble cast including Jackie Shroff, Arjun Rampal, Sonu Sood, and Harshvardhan Rane.

Actor Dipika Kakar turns 40 on August 6. While the television star has largely stayed away from fiction shows for the last four years, reports have recently surfaced that she may be making a return to the screen.According to India Today’s report, Dipika has been approached for a new fiction show under Ravi Dubey and Sargun Mehta’s production house Dreamiyata Entertainment. Actor Vivian Dsena is also reportedly in talks to play the male lead. However, neither of the actors nor the makers have confirmed any details so far.The speculation grew after Dipika resumed sharing regular vlogs on her YouTube channel, where she opened up about her ongoing recovery. However, in her recent Instagram live, she addressed the possibility of returning to work.“I had asked my doctor when I could return to television,” she said, adding that her original plan was to get back to acting once her son Ruhaan stopped breastfeeding and she regained her fitness. “My sudden cancer diagnosis changed everything,” she added.

title: Saurabh Sachdeva reveals ‘Maalik’ director was once his student
content:
Mumbai, July 24 (IANS) Actor Saurabh Sachdeva, who is known for his work in ‘Animal’, ‘Pushpa 2’, ‘Sacred Games’ and ‘Maalik’, has shared that the director of ‘Maalik’, Pulkit used to be his student.

Saurabh, who is also an acting coach, revealed that Pulkit started off as an actor, and later got into direction.

Also speaking about the director of the film, Pulkit, he said, “Pulkit was my student, a long time ago. Pulkit started as an actor, and I still remember, I used to live in Malad, and he came to my house one day while I was working with a few other actors. He said, ‘I don’t know what I want to do’. He was very unsure about his life and everything else. I said, ‘Take my camera, go to the park downstairs, and ask people why they come to the park. Go and record them’”.

“He took the camera and started recording. That was the seed of his desire to become a director. And he did become one. He made his first short film and casted me in it.It was a very beautiful film. Then he made another film, Maroon, and casted me again. Now this is going to be his first theatrical release. He told me, ‘This film is for you’. I said, ‘Alright, make it’. So, we started working”, he added.

He also spoke about his experience of working with Rajkumar Rao, and called him a “very open actor”. He shared that they were respecting each other’s space as actors.

He said, “We were allowing each other to be into each other’s space. I could get into his space easily; he could get into my space easily. There were no inhibitions, and there is a respect for the craft of each other. And yeah, long back his wife Patralekhaa was also my student, long, long back when I was with Mr. Barry sir, and that is the time she was my student”.

Meanwhile, Saurabh will be next seen in ‘Dhadak 2’.

--IANS

title: Russell Brand sued for £220k for failing to write self-help books
content:
Russell Brand is being sued for £220,000 after failing to write self-help books, according to reports.

Brand’s publishing deal with Pan Macmillan to write two books was pulled after a string of women came forward in 2023 alleging that Brand had sexually assaulted them. The 49-year-old comedian has denied all allegations against him.

Pan Macmillan has now filed to reclaim £220,000 of “wasted expenditure” from Brand and his company Pablo Diablo’s Legitimate Business Firm Ltd, The Times newspaper reported.

Brand is reported to have been offered £75,000 upfront for a first book, which was supposed to have been submitted by May 2021.

A payment of £142,000 was set for a second book, due out in October 2021. Brand was to get a further £179,500 on completion of both books.

title: The Godfather Director Francis Ford Coppola Hospitalised In Italy
content:
The Godfather Director Francis Ford Coppola Hospitalised In Italy

Francis Ford Coppola, a renowned Hollywood filmmaker has been hospitalised in Rome, Italy for a scheduled treatment after wrapping up his six-city US tour ahead of his upcoming release Megalopolis. His final show was a screening of the self-financed pic and a Q&A, took place at San Francisco’s Palace of Fine Arts on Friday night, before he flew for the scheduled checkup.

Francis Ford Coppola hospitalised for scheduled treatment

Francis Ford Coppola told SF Gate, "I am 85. I lost my wife [Eleanor Coppola] a year ago, around this time. But my attitude for death is that I always lived my life so that when I was at the moment approaching death, I wouldn’t say, ‘Oh, I wish I had done this and I wish I had done that.’ Instead, I say to myself, ‘I got to do this.’”

About his film Megalopolis

Directed, written and self-funded, Francis' Megalopolis had a special screening in the US theatres, attended by him in person. The film features an ensemble cast including Adam Driver, Giancarlo Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Shia LaBeouf, Jon Voight, Laurence Fishburne, Talia Shire, Jason Schwartzman, Kathryn Hunter, Grace VanderWaal, Chloe Fineman, James Remar, D. B. Sweeney, and Dustin Hoffman.

Francis talks about his upcoming potential project

As per reports surfacing online, the director will spend some time in Calabria city to look for newer locations to shoot his upcoming project which will not be like Godfather or Apocalypse Now and will focus on 'beautiful things about this region'.

Francis opens up about Apocalypse Now flop

In an interview with G2, he had mentioned, "Apocalypse Now was a big flop, it got terrible reviews, everyone said it was the worst movie ever made. And yet people never stopped going to see it. The same thing is now happening with Megalopolis.”

For the unversed, Megalopolis, which was earlier released in 2024, recently had a re-release where the director has added the deleted scenes to make the film 'weirder.'

title: Shatta Wale’s lamborghini seized by EOCO in link to financial crimes investigation
content:
6 hours ago

The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has confirmed conducting a legal search and seizure operation at the residence of Ghanaian dancehall artist, Charles Nii Armah Mensah, popularly known as Shatta Wale, in Trassaco Valley Phase 1.

The operation, carried out by EOCO's Surveillance and Asset Recovery Unit (SARU) in June 2025, was prompted by a 2023 request from the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Department of Justice (DOJ). This was part of an ongoing international investigation into financial crimes.

As a result of the operation, EOCO officers seized a 2019 Lamborghini Urus, which was reportedly linked to criminal proceeds belonging to Nana Kwabena Amuah, a Ghanaian currently serving an 86-month sentence in the U.S. for multiple financial offenses. Authorities in both the U.S. and Ghana claim the vehicle was purchased with illicit funds from Amuah’s criminal activities and had been traced to Shatta Wale.

EOCO has emphasised that the operation was conducted lawfully and smoothly, with officers described as “professional and civil” throughout the process.

Shatta Wale, according to sources, reportedly requested that the seizure not be made public, citing concerns that the vehicle was a key part of his brand image and that the publicity could harm his reputation. He voluntarily handed over the vehicle, which is now in EOCO’s custody.

Regarding the presence of armed officers during the operation, EOCO explained that it is standard procedure for SARU officers to be armed to ensure the safety of all involved in such high-stakes operations.

As part of the international investigation, the FBI and DOJ are preparing to send a formal Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) request to the Government of Ghana for the repatriation of the Lamborghini, which will aid in the recovery of a $4.7 million restitution ordered for Amuah’s crimes.

EOCO also revealed that both Shatta Wale and a former senior officer of Ghana’s National Signals Bureau (NSB) have been designated as persons of interest and are expected to be invited for questioning as part of the investigation.

Finally, EOCO stated that it may share the outcome of the investigation with the FBI and DOJ as part of its ongoing cooperation with international authorities.

title: Elon Musk joins wave of social media support for Novak Djokovic
content:
Novak Djokovic won an apology from an Australian TV presenter over 'insulting comments'. Image: Vince CALIGIURI / TENNIS AUSTRALIA / AFP

A leading TV presenter apologised on air Monday to Novak Djokovic after mocking the 24-time Grand Slam winner and Serbian fans at the Australian Open, with Elon Musk and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese among those wading into the row.

For the latest tennis news, bookmark The South African website’s dedicated section for free-to-read content

The 37-year-old tennis great refused to do a routine on-court interview after beating Jiri Lehecka to make the quarter-finals on Sunday evening in Melbourne.

Afterwards he said it was in protest at Tony Jones, a top sports presenter with host broadcaster Channel Nine, who he accused of “insulting and offensive comments” towards him and Serbian fans.

Jones had labelled Novak Djokovic a “has-been”, among other things, but said in his apology it was “banter”.

Novak Djokovic said he would boycott interviews with the TV station until he got an apology.

He later released a short video on X to explain his stance to fans, which has been viewed more than 60 million times and caught the attention of the site’s owner Musk.

“It’s way better just to talk to the public directly than go through the negativity filter of legacy media,” Musk posted in response, with Djokovic replying: “Indeed.”

Tennis names including former world number Boris Becker, Australian Nick Kyrgios, Jannik Sinner’s coach Darren Cahill and Grand Slam champion Victoria Azarenka all spoke out in support of Djokovic.

“The comments were made on the news on the Friday night, which I considered to be banter. I considered it to be humour, which is consistent with most things I do,” Jones said on Monday.

“Having said that, I was made aware on Saturday morning, from Tennis Australia via the Djokovic camp that the Djokovic camp was not happy at all with those comments.

“As such I immediately contacted the Djokovic camp and issued and apology to them – 48 hours ago – for any disrespect that Novak felt, that I had caused.

“As I stand here now I can only stand by that apology to Novak.”

‘Disrespect’

The veteran broadcaster was live at Melbourne Park on Friday when a large group of Novak Djokovic fans holding Serbian flags began cheering in the background behind him.

Jones responded by singing to them: “Novak, he’s overrated … Novak’s a has-been. Novak, kick him out.”

“I should also say the disrespect was extended, in many ways, to the Serbian fans,” he said in his apology.

Australian TV sports presenter Tony Jones at the Australian Open on Monday © Martin KEEP / AFP

“We have built up a nice rapport with the Serbian fans… there is banter, and I thought what I was doing was an extension of that banter. Quite clearly that has not been interpreted that way.

“I feel as though I’ve let down the Serbian fans. It has been an unfortunate situation.”

Channel Nine also apologised, saying “no harm was intended towards Novak or his fans”.

But in a strongly worded statement issued before Jones’s apology, the Serbian Council of Australia called for him to be sacked and said it had lodged a complaint with the Australian Human Rights Commission.

“His comments are offensive, racist and only serve to incite further discrimination of Australian-Serbs,” it said.

Australian Prime Minister Albanese urged more “kindness and generosity”.

“I’ve seen the comments made by (Jones),” he told ABC radio.

“We need more kindness and generosity and respect across the board. That’s what people are looking for.”

Jones was also a target for American player Danielle Collins last week after he labelled her a “brat” when she thanked Australian Open hecklers for “paying my bills” in her defeat of home hope Destanee Aiava.

Apology accepted, time to forgive and forget?

title: Gabrielle Union Reveals The ‘Stupid’ Purchase She Made After Earning Her First Big Paycheck
content:
Gabrielle Union made a name for herself in the best teen movies of the ‘90s, like She’s All That and 10 Things I Hate About You. We also can’t forget one of her most iconic roles as rival cheerleader, Isis, in Bring It On. But the American actress reveals that when she first started in Hollywood, she made a “stupid” purchase after earning her first paycheck.

When you receive a paycheck from a new job bigger than anything you’ve ever received before, it’s natural to want to go all out. After all, Chris Pratt admitted to blowing $75K he earned from his first big job, only to be surprised when it was all gone in two months.

Gabrielle Union certainly didn’t waste time with her big paycheck either. At the American Black Film Festival in Miami (via People ), the Being Mary Jane actress got real about the “stupid” purchase she made with her first paycheck. But as she was an up-and-coming actress at the time, I honestly find it understandable:

So stupid. I went on the Mazda lot. I’m like, ‘Oh, I’ve made it when I have a Mazda.’ My dad’s like, ‘Don’t buy a brand new car. It depreciates the second you drive it off the lot.’ I walked into Mazda and I bought myself a black on black Mazda Miata with leather seats. Lemme tell you about leather seats in Los Angeles. Do you know I scorched myself every time I got out? Yeah, that was my first purchase. And it depreciated the second I drove it off the lot!

A flaming hot car seat is definitely not fun to sit in on the road. You’d really have to invest in some windshield shades to prevent that from happening.

I totally see where Gabrielle Union was coming from, wanting to buy your dream car after receiving some major Hollywood moolah. But like Union's father told her, a new car can be a risky investment with the excitement fading as soon as you think about the upkeep, depreciation, and your back burning from the leather seats. Don’t you hate having to admit when your parents are right about something?

(Image credit: Universal Pictures)

While Gabrielle Union doesn’t mention which project came from her first big paycheck, I’d like to think she was talking about her unforgettable breakthrough performance in Bring It On. While She’s All That was Union’s first major movie role , she was more of a supporting character. Playing East Compton Clovers cheerleader Isis had her standing toe-to-toe with Kirsten Dunst and delivering fiercely snappy lines that would show that she's leading lady material. Given what an excellent performance she gave, I would say the Deliver Us From Eva actress deserved a hefty sum for it.

With Gabrielle Union now in her 50s, it makes sense why she’d look back at her first big paycheck purchase of a Mazda as “stupid.” But hey, we're only human. With all of the major movies she did early in her career and the excellent work that followed, Union’s value in Hollywood has only gone up. Working as an actress, producer, and her own successful business of hair products, the BET Award nominee has plenty of wins that can make her early big car purchase seem like an afterthought now.

title: New Who drummer Scott Devours: 'I know I need to earn this honor'
content:
Scott Devours, who is replacing Zak Starkey as the drummer of The Who, has shared his conflicting emotions over landing the job.

In an Instagram post and in the comments section, Devours, who's part of Roger Daltrey's solo band, says, "I understand and accept the reality that there are many lifelong Who fans who are absolutely gutted by the news that Zak is no longer on the throne behind The Who."

Noting that he's "processing this loss with a heavy heart too," Devours says, "It really is a strange contradiction of emotions to have the greatest moment of my professional career also be one framed with some sadness and shadowed by someone else’s loss."

Starkey announced on Sunday that he'd been fired a second time by The Who just two weeks after he was reinstated. He also claimed they asked him to say that he quit, but he refused.

Devours writes, "I'm sure there are many fans who will not accept me or anyone on that throne except for Zak. I know that this will be the case for some and I acknowledge that. ... The weight of this responsibility is enormous and I am feeling every ounce of it."

He goes on to say that he plans to honor the "legacy" of past drummers, including Zak, Kenney Jones, Simon Phillips and "the great Keith Moon."

He concludes by writing, "I know I need to earn this honor. Since this is the last time Pete and Roger will be touring the U.S., playing the greatest songs ever written, I will be giving them every second of my time, every beat of my heart, and every drop of my sweat and blood. This is my ultimate goal."

title: ‘South Park’ Owns White House With X-Rated Reply to ICE Post
authors: ["Cameron Adams", "Erkki Forster", "Catherine Bouris", "Cameron.Adams Thedailybeast.Com", "Got A Tip", "Send It To The Daily Beast", "The Daily Beast Podcast", "Ewan Palmer", "Eboni Boykin-Patterson", "Corbin Bolies"]
content:
South Park has annihilated the White House after the Trump administration repurposed their cartoon parody of immigration officers on an official government social media account.

On Tuesday, the Department of Homeland Security’s X account used an animated image of ICE officers from this week’s South Park episode in an attempt to recruit staff.

Hours later, on their X account on Tuesday, South Park reposted the DHS video with the caption, “Wait, so we ARE relevant?” The post then suggested the department, “#eatabagofd---s.”

It comes just two weeks after the White House slammed South Park as irrelevant and a “fourth-rate show.”

Following the season premiere of the comedy that depicted Donald Trump with a micro-penis, the White House claimed South Park “hasn’t been relevant for over 20 years and is hanging on by a thread with uninspired ideas in a desperate attempt for attention.”

‘South Park’ responds. Comedy Central

In a statement to the Daily Beast about the latest comment, a DHS Spokesperson said, “We want to thank South Park for drawing attention to ICE law enforcement recruitment: We are calling on patriotic Americans to help us remove murderers, gang members, pedophiles, and other violent criminals from our country.”

The statement then included details for recruitment and benefits on offer for signing up.

The website, which offers a potential $50,000 signing bonus, states “America has been invaded by criminals and predators. We need YOU to get them out. You do not need an undergraduate degree.”

The White House referred the Daily Beast to the Department of Homeland Security. The Daily Beast has also contacted Comedy Central for comment.

The next South Park episode is titled “Got a Nut” and airs this Wednesday.

A photo from the episode appears to show character Mr. Mackey now working as an ICE officer after losing his job as school counselor. He is standing next to South Park’s take on secretary of homeland security Kristi Noem.

“When Mr. Mackay loses his job, he desperately tries to find a new way to make a living,” the episode’s description reads.

Mr Mackey and South Park's Kristi Noem in a new episode. Comedy Central

The episode is also set to feature regular character Cartman channelling MAGA mouthpiece Charlie Kirk, demonstrating the comedy has no plans of shying away from parodying the Trump Administration despite being blasted by the White House.

Kirk embraced the joke and told Fox News Digital, “I think it’s kind of funny and it kind of goes to show the cultural impact and the resonance that our movement has been able to achieve. So I look at this as a badge of honor.”

Cartman as a version of Turning Points USA founder Charlie Kirk on Season 27, Episode 2 of “South Park.” Comedy Central

The July 23 season 27 return saw South Park achieve their highest season opener ratings since 1999. “Sermon on the ‘Mount’” had nearly 6 million viewers three days after its premiere. It was the most-watched show on all cable channels on its debut day.

This week, Deadline reported that George Cheeks, the CEO who was in charge during the Trump-approved cancellation of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert will now be in charge of South Park.

Cheeks will oversee the edgy comedy since the billion-dollar merger between Paramount and Skydance, which had to be approved by the Trump administration.

Last month, South Park creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone signed a $1.5 billion deal, just prior to the merger, purely for the streaming rights to their content.

title: Hytale co-founder replies to their own "no risk, no story" tweet, and fans haven't known peace since: "This is either the biggest comeback in the gaming industry or the biggest troll ever"
content:
Hytale fans are scrambling to decode the meaning behind a single emoji tweeted by its original co-founder, Simon Collins-Laflamme.

He's been saying he wants to buy back the IP of the Minecraft -inspired survival game from Riot after the League of Legends company cancelled it . Early this morning (or late last night, depending on your timezone), though, Collins-Laflamme tweeted a smiley face with sunglasses in response to his June 29 tweet, "no risk, no story." Now, fans are desperate to know what it means.

"This is either the biggest comeback in the gaming industry or the biggest troll ever. There's truly no in between," one redditor writes . "Simon already has Hytale back and he is preparing this massive reveal, but he is just as excited as us so he decided to foreshadow the comeback just a bit. Guys I'm not crazy please hear me out."

I think it's unlikely Collins-Laflamme already has the IP again, unless he has started talks with Riot unbelievably quickly. He did say an IP buy-back would be the quickest and easiest way to get control of the game again, but this still seems too soon.

Others are simply replying with memes about hopium , praying the emoji signifies good news. "If this somehow happens it will surpass even No Man's Sky as the biggest gaming comeback ever," writes one hopeful fan.

Everyone should temper their expectations. Collins-Laflamme has stated that if he does manage to get hold of the IP, " a lot of content will be getting cut early on " so that the game can first be launched in early access as quickly as possible.

Personally, I think the emoji just means things are going well. That or he's drumming up hype to better help him in negotiations with Riot. What do you think?

title: Rod Wave Arrested On Assault And Gun Charges In ATL
content:
Rod Wave is facing serious legal trouble after being arrested in Fulton County, Georgia, on Tuesday, May 21. According to AllHipHop, the Florida native was taken into custody on a slew of felony charges stemming from an alleged incident that occurred a month earlier on April 21.

Court records indicate the 25-year-old artist, born Rodarius Green, is now facing 13 felony counts, including aggravated assault, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, pointing a gun at another person, criminal damage to property, reckless conduct, and tampering with physical evidence. He was later released after posting surety bonds for the charges.

At this time, details surrounding the April incident remain unclear. However, online speculation suggests the situation may involve his girlfriend, social media personality Mini Barbie, also known as Nari. Unconfirmed rumors circulating online allege that Rod Wave may have fired a weapon at her or her vehicle, though law enforcement has yet to address these claims publicly.

The arrest follows a recent public clash between Mini Barbie and Dee, the mother of Rod Wave’s two daughters. The heated back-and-forth played out on Twitter in March, after a fan account posted a collage of women linked to the rapper. A comment from one of Mini Barbie’s alleged friends sparked the online feud, leading to a fiery exchange between the two women.

Neither Rod Wave nor his representatives have issued a statement regarding the arrest. No court dates have been announced as of yet, and the investigation into the alleged April incident remains ongoing.

title: Bad Bunny Claps Back: Singer Defends Being the Super Bowl Halftime Show Performer in Fierce 'SNL' Monologue
content:
Article continues below advertisement

Bad Bunny, the Puerto Rican hitmaker, addressed critics who questioned his selection as headliner for the Super Bowl 2026 Halftime Show during his recent appearance on Saturday Night Live. He turned the scorn into a moment of empowerment, reinforcing his belief in the significance of his performance for Latin culture.

Article continues below advertisement

Bad Bunny speaks about his Super Bowl performance in Spanish at end of SNL monologue:



“If you didn’t understand what I just said, you have 4 months to learn.” pic.twitter.com/bT5ujmmh3P — Pop Crave (@PopCrave) October 5, 2025

Article continues below advertisement

Source: @SNL/X Bad Bunny spoke out during his 'SNL' monologue on October 4.

Article continues below advertisement

“You might not know this, but I’m doing the Super Bowl Halftime Show. And I’m very happy and I think everybody’s happy about it,” Bad Bunny asserted, humorously adding, “Even Fox News!” This bold proclamation was met with laughter from the live audience. His monologue took a sharp turn when NBC aired a montage of Fox News hosts declaring their “love” for Bad Bunny, humorously framing them as unlikely supporters of the artist. “Bad Bunny is my favorite musician and he should be the next president,” the hosts enthusiastically claimed in the clip, driving home the ironic angle of mainstream media embracing an artist who represents a significant portion of the Latino community.

Article continues below advertisement

Source: MEGA Bad Bunny said he's 'excited' to be 'doing the Super Bowl.'

Want OK! each day? Sign up here!

Article continues below advertisement

“I’m really excited to be doing the Super Bowl,” the Grammy-winning artist continued. “I know that people all around the world who love my music are also happy… especially all of the Latinos and Latinas in the world here in the United States who have worked to open doors.” In the spirit of inclusivity, Bad Bunny switched to Spanish mid-monologue to emphasize the cultural importance of the event, stating, “It's more than a win for myself, it’s a win for all of us. Our footprints and our contribution in this country, no one will ever be able to take that away or erase it.” With that, he concluded his powerful statement, reminding detractors of the rich cultural contributions of the Latino community to the United States.

Article continues below advertisement

Source: MEGA The singer has gotten backlash after he was announced as the performer.

The past week had seen a flurry of negative comments aimed at the "Tití Me Preguntó" singer since the announcement of his Super Bowl gig, which will be on February 8, 2026, at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. Notably, former racecar driver Danica Patrick weighed in, suggesting that Bad Bunny, who primarily sings in Spanish, should not headline one of America's biggest televised events. Her comment, which drew ire from fans, asserted that “no songs in English should be allowed at one of America’s highest-rated television events of the year… not just for sports.”
